articles.title: “He probably won’t get a chance”: Tyreek Hill’s potential return to the Chiefs faces a major roadblock as NFL insider shares concerning update
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has been facing a lot of uncertainties concerning his comeback to the field.
articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has been facing a lot of uncertainties concerning his comeback to the field. While his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has assured that Tyreek Hill will be back on the field in no time, there have been no developments yet. Amid this, it seems there could be a chance that Tyreek Hill does not go back to the Kansas City Chiefs.NFL insider makes an update about whether a potential reunion between Kansas City Chiefs and Tyreek Hill is possibleA few hours ago, Billy Heyen of Heavy noted in a recent report, “The Chiefs may have moved themselves out of the picture less than half an hour before Tuesday's trade deadline. That's when they traded for Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts.”Billy Heyen of Heavy added, “Downs is a slot receiver and another quality target for Patrick Mahomes. But the arrival of Downs lessens the potential need for Hill. Hill might still be a few weeks away in his injury recovery, based on the latest comments from his agent, Drew Rosenhaus. When he's ready, though, he probably won't get a chance with Kansas City.”Neither Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus nor the Kansas City Chiefs has responded to this yet.Tyreek Hill stays away from commenting on reunion rumors with the Chiefs as things remain uncertain in his careerOver the last few weeks, there have been many conflicting reports of Tyreek Hill potentially returning to the Kansas City Chiefs.While some have predicted that there is a high chance it can happen, others have consistently denied it.A few weeks ago, while speaking to The Athletic's Mike Silver, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce reflected on Tyreek Hill’s situation with the Kansas City Chiefs as he said, "That's out of my hands, but I know I'd love to have 'The Cheetah' back in this building," tight end Travis Kelce told "He's a brother.”The star player added, “He's one of those people who, when he sets his mind to something, he usually delivers. You saw that with Miami, when all the haters were saying he couldn't play and he went and had his best year. I'd be excited by what he could do (here)."The team’s popular quarterback Patrick Mahomes added, "I have no idea (if signing Hill would happen), but it'd be pretty cool…”Across six seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs (2016–2021), Tyreek Hill recorded 479 receptions for 6,630 receiving yards, 67 total touchdowns (56 receiving, 6 rushing, 5 return), six Pro Bowl selections, three First-Team All-Pro honors, and a Super Bowl LIV championship.However, the 32 year old popular wide receiver Tyreek Hill has mostly kept himself away from these comments as he has focused on making a comeback to the field after the severe injuries he sustained in the last season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' new Chiefs teammate Josh Downs has one goal that could quickly make him a Kansas City favorite
articles.summary: Josh Downs has been a Chief for only a few days, and he already knows what could slow him down: the playbook.
articles.body: Josh Downs has been a Chief for only a few days, and he already knows what could slow him down: the playbook. The slot receiver came over from the 2-7 Colts at the trade deadline and now joins a 6-2 team with Super Bowl plans. His goal is plain, and it has nothing to do with stats. Learn the offense fast and earn Patrick Mahomes’ trust. Kansas City has seen deadline pickups fade before, and Downs told reporters this week he does not plan to join that list.Downs wants to win over Mahomes by learning the playbook fastThe Chiefs have a mixed record with midseason arrivals. In 2024, DeAndre Hopkins was busy early and then tapered off. Josh Uche never found a real role. Kansas City additions tend to hit a steep learning curve.Downs is a short-area specialist who works mostly from the slot. That puts him in the same lane as Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice, who already get a lot of that work. The offense also leans on choice and option routes, so a receiver has to read the defense and know what Mahomes expects.Rookie Cyrus Allen shows the risk. Nine games into his Chiefs tenure, his role trails the hype, partly because he has not fully mastered the offense.Downs says he gets that, and he started with his quarterback.“Build that relationship with him and then on the field, when he throws me the ball, just catch it,” Downs said. “And keep making plays when he throws it to me. Just do anything I can to learn the offense as fast as possible. I don’t want to be a guy that’s asking everybody what the play is [or] what the formation is. I feel like that’s when you kind of get left behind, so I want to do everything I can to learn as fast as possible.”Downs leaves the Colts with no hard feelingsDowns also moves from the 2-7 Colts to a 6-2 club with title hopes.“It’s great to join a team like this with so much history and so much winning in their past, and even now,” Downs said. “So I’m excited to be able to be a part of a group like this and contribute where I can.”The numbers back him up. Over three and a half years in Indianapolis, Downs drew 350 targets and caught 231 passes for 2,494 yards and 12 touchdowns. He posted a 66.0% catch rate and a 50.6% success rate. His second season may have been his best overall, and he stayed effective last year on 6% fewer snaps than the year before.He asked out, and Indianapolis granted it. Downs has no complaints.“I know they made a decision based off the betterment of their organization,” Downs said. “I respect them for sending me to an organization like this. Those are great people over there, and I feel like they did right by me. This is the choice they made.”Catching the ball was never his problem. Knowing where to be before the snap is the test, and Mahomes will notice quickly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 6 Trades We Wish We Had Seen at the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. And while it still doesn't generate the kind of frenzy we see in the NBA or MLB, it's busier than it used to be.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. And while it still doesn't generate the kind of frenzy we see in the NBA or MLB, it's busier than it used to be.

The Chicago Bears sent a pair of first-rounders to Tennessee for Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. The Jacksonville Jaguars used their first two picks in next year's draft (and then some) to bolster the defense with the acquisitions of safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis. The Indianapolis Colts essentially traded away their wideout corps—but puzzlingly decided not to deal their star running back despite a lost season.

Those were just some of the biggest developments at the deadline. There were plenty of other deals. Some minor. Some with the potential for a major impact. But there were also trades we would have liked to see—deals that made sense but never came to pass.

New York Giants Receive: RB Jonathan Taylor

Indianapolis Colts Receive: 2027 Round 2 Pick, 2027 Round 5 Pick

The Indianapolis Colts are a ship without a captain right now after the firing of general manager Chris Ballard on October 19.

That didn't stop the Colts from dealing wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the deadline. But it may have contributed to the team holding onto running back Jonathan Taylor—a non-move Indy may come to regret.

Per ESPN's Jordan Raanan , Fox Sports reported that the running back-needy New York Giants offered the Colts a second-round pick and a fifth-round pick for Taylor.

The Giants subsequently withdrew the offer, though head coach John Harbaugh left the door open to further talks while stressing that any deal had to make sense for the team's present and future.

"I'm not just going to go for a short-term fix at exorbitant cost. That's not where we're at," he said. "And usually when you do that sort of thing, it doesn't work out for you."

Now, the Giants still need a running back, and an Indianapolis team staring at a ground-up rebuild has a running back with more than 1,700 career NFL carries on a deal averaging $22 million annually.

The Colts should have taken the best offer they could get for Taylor and moved on. They're unlikely to do better in the offseason.

Green Bay Packers Receive: RB Tony Pollard

Tennessee Titans Receive: 2027 Round 3 Pick

On one hand, it appeared to make sense for the Tennessee Titans to trade veteran running back Tony Pollard. At 1-7, the Titans have little reason to prioritize short-term results. Pollard is in the last year of his contract.

As Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated reported ahead of the deadline, Tennessee was reluctant to trade Pollard, 29, because of his role in helping the team evaluate quarterback Cam Ward:

"Tennessee, as we've said the last few weeks, values him in how he's helping the team evaluate Cam Ward. So, they're not going to give him away. Thus, it'd take at least a fourth-rounder, and maybe a third to get him out of there—as the offense has improved, it's become harder for the brass to reckon with letting him go."

A late Day 2 pick is a hefty price to pay for a 29-year-old back on an expiring contract. But given the Green Bay Packers' playoff ambitions, the potential short-term upgrade could have justified the cost.

Green Bay ranks last in the NFL in rushing at just 68.2 yards per game. The offensive line bears some responsibility for those struggles, but the backs have also underperformed—and Josh Jacobs is now out indefinitely with a broken finger.

As the Los Angeles Rams have shown—and the Jacksonville Jaguars are trying to demonstrate this year—a willingness to trade draft capital for immediate help can strengthen a contender's chances.

Los Angeles Rams Receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr.

Jacksonville Jaguars Receive: 2027 Round 2 Pick

With his offensive role all but evaporated in Jacksonville, there was plenty of speculation that the Jaguars would look to deal wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.

However, the trade deadline came and went without a deal, and Jaguars general manager James Gladstone told reporters that the team wasn't interested in moving the 24-year-old.

"We have a ton of value when it comes to BTJ," he said. "His role and what I imagine his contribution is going to be [is] notable. He's such a good person to work with, such a good teammate, and so I expect a lot of good that comes in what lies in front."

"Notable" is an interesting word to use when it comes to Thomas' role: His target share has dropped from 25.3 percent in his breakout 2024 season to 9.5 percent this year. Last week against the Baltimore Ravens, he wasn't targeted once—the first time in his career that had happened.

With both Davante Adams and Puka Nacua out indefinitely, the win-now Rams are as desperate as any team in the league for wideout help. This would be an aggressive deal—sending a second-rounder to Jacksonville would wipe out the first two days of the 2027 draft for Los Angeles.

But at 5-4, the Rams don't have a lot of margin for error this season. And there isn't a general manager in the league who has been more willing to sacrifice the future for the present in recent years than Les Snead.

Edge Danielle Hunter to San Francisco 49ers

San Francisco 49ers Receive: Edge Danielle Hunter

Houston Texans Receive: 2027 Round 2 Pick, 2028 Round 5 Pick

To be clear, there was never any real indication that the Houston Texans ever entertained the idea of trading veteran edge-rusher Danielle Hunter.

Despite a woeful start to the season, the Texans actually added a player in wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., and at 3-5 Houston appears to believe it is still in the hunt for a playoff spot.

However, just because the Texans didn't consider dealing Hunter doesn't mean they shouldn't have—and if the 32-year-old did become available, the 49ers would have been an obvious fit.

At 7-1, San Francisco has the best record in the NFC. But the team's pass rush has been hit-or-miss this year. The team has just 15 sacks this season—only four NFL teams have fewer.

With $35.5 million in cap space, per Spotrac , San Francisco has the wiggle room to absorb Hunter's sizable contract. He has just four sacks in eight games this year, but in four straight seasons from 2022 to 2025 the five-time Pro Bowler recorded at least 10.5 sacks.

Pairing Hunter with Nick Bosa on the edge could have turned San Francisco's biggest defensive weakness into a strength. While losing Hunter would have been a blow to the Texans, trading him could have helped them recoup the draft capital they spent on Harrison.

Los Angeles Chargers Receive: 2028 Round 4 Pick, 2028 Round 5 Pick (from Titans)

The Los Angeles Chargers' decision to stand pat at the deadline is difficult to reconcile with their winless start.

The 2026 season has been a catastrophe in Los Angeles. But despite being the only winless team in the league, the Chargers essentially stood pat at the trade deadline. There were rumblings that teams had interest in veteran edge-rusher Khalil Mack, but per Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network , the Bolts weren't interested.

"The Chargers never wanted to deal Khalil Mack. They never got close to dealing Khalil Mack," Rapoport said. "They wanted him in their locker room, they want him to help teach some of the young pass-rushers. They just want a good culture, and he is a great guy and a great leader."

Mack's leadership has value, but with the Chargers at 0-8 and the 35-year-old playing on a one-year deal, acquiring draft capital would have been the more practical long-term move.

The Chicago Bears were already wildly aggressive in upgrading the defensive line, sending two first-round picks and a 2027 fourth-rounder to Tennessee for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-rounder.

That fifth-rounder could have been included in a package to bolster the pass rush—with a player who spent four seasons in Chicago.

The Chargers should have been stockpiling picks wherever possible. And the Bears may come to regret not taking their win-now mentality all the way.

Arizona Cardinals Receive: 2027 Round 3 Pick, 2028 Round 4 Pick

With the Arizona Cardinals struggling, there was reason to expect them to be sellers at the trade deadline.

The Buffalo Bills came to the Cardinals with a hefty offer for veteran safety Budda Baker but were rebuffed, according to Easton Freeze of A to Z Sports:

"The Bills went to the Cardinals first. Bills GM Brandon Beane was dealing with Arizona about Baker, reportedly with an offer centered around strong second-round value. Every single person I talked to yesterday agreed that it was flat-out baffling that the Cardinals turned that down. It reeks of a foolish ownership decision."

The Bills pivoted to Amani Hooker, making a similar offer that the Titans accepted. Arizona, meanwhile, passed up an opportunity to acquire draft capital for the future despite its current struggles.

Still, the Bills aren't the only playoff contender with issues in the secondary. The Detroit Lions recently got Brian Branch back on the field, but their pass defense continues to struggle—they allow more passing yards per game than any other team in the league.

Pairing Branch with Baker wouldn't solve Detroit's issues at cornerback, but it could give the Lions one of the league's best safety duos. The move would also give Baker an opportunity to help a playoff contender down the stretch.

articles.title: First Super Bowl? Ranking Each NFL Team's Likelihood to Win First Lombardi This Year
articles.summary: Exactly 20 NFL franchises have won at least one Super Bowl—a number that hasn't changed since the Philadelphia Eagles finally joined that club at the conclusion of the 2017 season.
articles.body:
Exactly 20 NFL franchises have won at least one Super Bowl—a number that hasn't changed since the Philadelphia Eagles finally joined that club at the conclusion of the 2017 season.

However, according to FanDuel odds , five of the top 12 Super Bowl favorites have never won the Vince Lombardi Trophy.

Let's look at those five, along with the seven other Super Bowl-less teams, and their chances of breaking through in Los Angeles on Feb. 14.

Although the Cardinals have beaten the Rams and Cowboys on the road, their roster is falling apart at 3-6 as they prepare to start a rookie quarterback for the first time in Week 10. They're three games out of a playoff spot in the NFC and have lost 10 consecutive home games dating back to last September. The rebuild trudges on.

At 0-8, even winning each of their last nine games probably wouldn't get the Chargers into the playoffs. See ya next year.

It's almost the same scenario for the 1-7 Titans, which is compounded by the fact that they sold off two major defensive pieces at the deadline. The team is realistically focused on 2027 and beyond.

At 3-6, they're in the same wild-card jam as the Cardinals. However, a playoff path remains open in the comically weak NFC South, keeping their faint hopes alive. This roster has plenty of talent, but the quarterback position remains unstable. The reality is they're still completing a rebuild.

They sit atop that aforementioned comically weak division via tiebreaker at 3-5. They did gain some critical postseason experience when they almost toppled the Rams last January. Still, we're talking about a team with a bottom-five defense that has lost three in a row.

It was never really about 2026 for these Browns, who greatly exceeded expectations early but have now crashed back to earth via back-to-back losses to the Steelers and Saints. They're 5-4, but with a minus-35 scoring margin, they've averaged just 16.0 points per game over the last five weeks.

The 3-5 Texans deserve a much better shot than the 5-4 Browns or division-leading Panthers, mainly because of talent and momentum. We know what Houston brings to the table defensively. C.J. Stroud is having an impeccably timed career year for a squad that hasn't lost in regulation since Week 4. It's not entirely out of the realm of possibility for them to stay hot, sneak in and go on their first-ever Super Bowl run. But it's still a heck of a mountain to climb considering their early hole.

They have three more wins than Houston but are moving in the opposite direction and are stuck in a division from hell. Minnesota's quarterback problem became urgent after consecutive losses in which they scored a grand total of 21 points and fell to 6-2. Still, the defense is stacked, and at least Kirk Cousins gives them some reason for hope under center, so you can't shut the door on them just yet.

The 6-2 Lions have the talent on both sides of the ball and are riding a four-game winning streak. However, they're stuck battling Chicago, Minnesota and Green Bay in the NFC North. It's worth flagging the fact that they've faced the easiest schedule in the NFL, per ESPN's Football Power Index . That will change down the stretch, but there's no doubt the Lions are in the mix.

It still isn't easy to trust these Bengals, but they certainly have the offensive talent. They're led by the MVP frontrunner at quarterback. They haven't lost since Week 4, scoring more than 30 points in every game over a four-game winning streak to emerge as the clear-cut betting favorite in the AFC North at 6-2. Given their soft second-half schedule and momentum, the top seed in the AFC is within reach. Once you have that, you're a major player.

The league's top-rated team in terms of DVOA (defense-adjusted value over average) and point differential (plus-108, towering over second-place San Francisco at plus-79) just got a lot better at the deadline. It's really coming together in every aspect. The path is quite clear following a 6-2 start. The only question is: Are they ready?

The Bills are holding down the top seed in the AFC with a 7-1 record. They were buyers at the deadline. Josh Allen is a prime MVP candidate, as he is definitely further along in his career than Trevor Lawrence. In fact, this Buffalo team is altogether more experienced and mature than the Jags. This very well could be the year it finally happens for the league's top offensive squad. Then again, we've been fooled by them before.

articles.title: Week 10 Waiver Wire Best Pickups and Sleepers With FAAB Analysis, Predictions
articles.summary: Week 10 is already underway and waiver claims have been processed in most fantasy leagues. However, it may not be too late to find help in free agency—and many managers will need fill-ins this week.
articles.body:
Week 10 is already underway and waiver claims have been processed in most fantasy leagues. However, it may not be too late to find help in free agency—and many managers will need fill-ins this week.

The injury hits keep coming, with Arizona Cardinals receiver Michael Wilson becoming the latest fantasy star to land on season-ending injured reserve. Additionally, the Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers have the week off.

This means that standouts like Caleb Williams, Saquon Barkley, Bucky Irving, and Jonah Coleman are unavailable.

Here, we'll examine some top waiver options who may still be free to sign, run down some free agent acquisition budget (FAAB) guidelines for leagues with weekend waivers, and make a few statistical predictions.

The list of viable starting quarterbacks available on the wire this week is quite short. Malik Willis just went to injured reserve, and Drew Lock is dealing with an obliques injury. Kirk Cousins has been heavily targeted since being traded to the Minnesota Vikings, and Fernando Mendoza will make his first start against a tough Seattle Seahawks defense.

However, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers is only rostered in 41 percent of fantasy leagues and has a fair matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals.

The Bengals have surrendered an average of 17.9 fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks. While the Steelers have leaned heavily on their ground game recently, they may need Rodgers to throw early and often to keep pace with Joe Burrow and Co.

Rodgers is a mid-level streamer who should have a good amount of insurance/backup value moving forward as well. He's worth roughly three percent of an FAAB budget right now.

Week 10 Projection: 280 passing yards, 2 TDs, 12 rushing yards

Kenneth Walker III is unquestionably the star of the Kansas City Chiefs' rushing attack. However, Andy Reid has done a fine job of incorporating rookie Emmett Johnson into the offense, especially over the last couple of weeks.

Johnson was a big part of the receiving game two weeks ago against Denver, and he finished with a whopping 25.3 fantasy points. He was a change-of-pace runner last week and tallied a respectable 9.4 fantasy points. He should see a fair bit of action this week as the Chiefs take on the Atlanta Falcons.

The Falcons, by the way, have surrendered the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

Johnson is still available in over 70 percent of fantasy leagues. However, managers should consider targeting him fairly aggressively (5-8% of FAAB budget), as he's one of the top handcuffs in the league.

Week 10 Projection: 42 rushing yards, 3 receptions, 33 receiving yards

Following a devastating knee injury that cost him all of the 2025 season, Tank Dell is back in the lineup for the Houston Texans. Following a relatively quiet 2026 debut, Dell fully announced his return against the Los Angeles Chargers last week.

On Sunday, Dell recorded four catches for 105 yards, a touchdown, and 20.5 fantasy points.

Dell may not be quite as productive this week against a solid Cleveland Browns defense, but he should have a reasonable PPR floor. Nico Collins is likely to draw a lot of Denzel Ward in coverage, which could regularly leave Dell open on underneath routes.

The 27-year-old is dealing with hand and shoulder injuries, so Dell's status will be worth watching. However, he should be a strong flex option moving forward and is worth well over five percent of FAAB. He's currently rostered in 38 percent of leagues.

Week 10 Projection: 6 receptions, 67 yards

Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth has a limited ceiling, largely because fellow tight end Darnell Washington exists. The mammoth Washington sees a lot of the red-zone work, and Freiermuth hasn't caught a touchdown pass since Week 5.

Freiermuth, who is rostered in 38 percent of leagues, is still worth around five percent of FAAB, though. He's a high-volume target who has reached double-digit fantasy points in three of his last five games. With Pittsburgh's bye out of the way, he'll also be a sound backup option for the remainder of the season.

This week, Freiermuth should have an excellent chance to eclipse 10 fantasy points again. As previously noted, Pittsburgh may have to pass frequently. The Bengals' defense has been susceptible to tight ends.

Cincinnati has surrendered the ninth-most fantasy points to the position this season.

Week 10 Projection: 5 receptions, 57 yards

articles.title: The 10 Most Underrated Prospects in 2027 NFL Draft
articles.summary: As the 2026 college football regular season enters its final month, with conference championship games set to finish on Dec. 12, the on-field portion of NFL draft evaluations are nearing completion.
articles.body:
As the 2026 college football regular season enters its final month, with conference championship games set to finish on Dec. 12, the on-field portion of NFL draft evaluations are nearing completion.

However, plenty can still be achieved during these final few appearances, with a handful of prospects primed to rise throughout the remaining process.

The Bleacher Report Scouting Department identified 10 prospects who don't currently hold a first-round grade—the site's grading scale can be seen courtesy of its previous player rankings—but could find themselves in that range before next April's event.

Upside and potential are euphemisms often used throughout the scouting process. In essence, the scouting process is searching for those candidates who will continue to ascend, raise their stock and see their talent translate to the professional level. Each of those listed here has an outstanding opportunity to fall into that category.

The NFL loves versatility. Michigan's Smith Snowden can contribute in multiple areas.

Prior to arriving at Michigan, Snowden contributed in the Utah Utes' secondary, as a kick returner and even sprinkled in a few carries at running back along the way.

Currently, Jyaire Hill is the Wolverines' highest-graded cornerback prospect. He'll likely stay that way, while holding a late first-round/early second-round projection. However, Snowden's ability to be a multifaceted defensive chess piece and all-around athlete will almost certainly intrigue NFL organizations.

Snowden could contribute at outside corner, work over the slot or find a home as a full-time safety depending on his next team's plans. Questions about size, lack of length and top-end speed must be answered throughout the predraft process.

Still, a positionless defender capable of contributing in multiple roles, while staying on the field for all three downs, tends to hold a premium.

Without looking, which prospect leads all tight ends in touchdown receptions? North Carolina's Jelani Thurman, of course.

After three seasons with the Ohio State Buckeyes, where he was a limited contributor, Thurman has blossomed after transferring to the Tar Heels program. The 6'6", 250-pound underclassman's natural size, athleticism and explosiveness have allowed him to thrive this fall.

Thurman already set career highs with 45 receptions and 525 yards. He'll continue to add to those numbers over UNC's next three games (and a possible bowl appearance).

This year's draft class showed how increased usage of multiple-tight end sets among NFL schemes will elevate the value of the position.

Thurman's skill set still includes significant growth potential, specifically as a pure pass-catcher, which will further increase his desirability at the next level.

Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore has been on the first-round fringe for the entirety of the current draft cycle.

An understanding developed that he has the potential to be, at bare minimum, a quality rotational pass-rusher. This season has proved the senior prospect can be an every-down defender at the next level.

Obviously, the ability to rush the passer maintains a high premium. In Traore's case, a more well-rounded skill set is what makes him undervalued compared to the previous projection.

Traore plays with more sand at the point of attack than his 6'5", 253-pound frame indicates. Second, he can still use his quickness to beat offensive linemen off the snap and shoot gaps. Third, he's fluid enough to drop into coverage and not look out of place.

An elite pass-rusher always has an edge over others at his position, but NFL teams also want every-down defensive linemen who can defend the run as well as rush the passer.

Traore already showed he shouldn't just be looked at as a first-round possibility based purely on his ability to turn the edge. He can also set the edge and do far more within a defensive scheme.

This year's tight end class is rather intriguing. As mentioned, TEs were highly valued in the 2026 draft, with eight being selected during the second day.

Next year's group may be even more talented overall, with Luke Reynolds serving as a prime example.

After two seasons with the Penn State Nittany Lions, Reynolds transferred to Virginia Tech and emerged as an elite receiving threat. The Hokie currently leads all tight ends with 56 receptions. For comparison, Reynolds has only 13 fewer catches than Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith and six more than Indiana's Charlie Becker—both of whom are considered future top-10 draft picks.

Reynolds' ability to locate passes, contort his body and then flash ultra-reliable hands stand out regarding the junior's game. He's not as big or as athletic as the aforementioned Jelani Thurman. However, Reynolds' skill set portends a long-time productive target working the middle of the field as a professional quarterback's best friend.

Current B/R Ranking : 45th Grade : 7.7 Offensive tackles tend to rise naturally throughout the evaluation process due to their positional value. NFL organizations are always looking for incoming blockers capable of playing and staying on an island. Kentucky's Lance Heard is definitely one who opened eyes this fall.

Heard presents the requisite size (6'6", 325 lbs) and length to remain at offensive tackle. The two-time transfer, who began his career at LSU, started two seasons for the Tennessee Volunteers before landing at Kentucky for his final campaign.

Heard's growth with his hand-usage has been particularly impressive. He always flashed the physical capabilities to play the position. Now, he regularly uses his size and length to his advantage by establishing first meaningful contact.

The Wildcats' blindside protector may not be an elite athlete and plays somewhat upright, but he understands his strengths and how to weaponize them. Thus, he's the type of offensive line prospect capable of becoming a Year 1 NFL starter.

Current B/R Ranking : 54th Grade : 7.7 The NFL can't get enough wide receivers, especially those with size and obvious ways to win at the next level. Arizona State's Reed Harris is a 6'5", 220-pound target. He's currently tied for third among wide receivers with 50 or more receptions, alongside Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, by averaging 17.4 yards per catch. In some ways, Harris brings a Drake London-like presence due to his combination of size and history as a basketball player. Much like London, the Sun Devil is more fluid than the majority of bigger wide receivers. Harris is capable of sinking his hips and running good routes, despite not being an overly explosive target. Still, he knows how to use his frame to his advantage, either by gaining leverage against defenders or bodying them in contested-catch situations. Considering Rutgers' KJ Duff is now out for the season with an ankle injury, Harris now has a pathway to be an NFL team's preferred big-bodied target once Jeremiah Smith and Charlie Becker are off the board early in next year's draft.

Current B/R Ranking : 42nd Grade : 7.8 During this past draft cycle, a former Utah Ute, Spencer Fano, emerged as OL1 and a top-10 draft pick. Current left tackle Zereoue Williams probably won't claim the former in a class that features LSU's Jordan Seaton, but he still has a shot at the latter. With both of Utah's offensive tackles hearing their names called during this year's first round, Williams finally had an opportunity this fall to become a starter for the first time and he's excelled. The 6'8", 305-pound sixth-year senior has made the most of his final collegiate season, emerging as a fluid pass-blocker with the upside to become a starting NFL left tackle. He has the size, length and movement skills to hit his set points and redirect against movement. Plus, his height doesn't negatively impact his run-blocking. Williams was forced to bide his time and deal with a significant injury in 2023, but his patience and persistence have paid off in a big way.

Current B/R Ranking : 31st Grade : 7.9 Xavier Gilliam is yet another transfer student who has thrived in new surroundings. So much so, the interior defender could easily work his way into being a top-15 draft pick when it's all said and done. Gilliam found himself in a rotational role as part of the Penn State Nittany Lions' defensive front during his first two seasons. He's become a dominant player as the tip of the spear for the Tennessee Volunteers' defense. The 6'2", 305-pound defensive tackle has the quickness off the snap to consistently reset the line of scrimmage, collapse the pocket and cause general havoc in opposing backfields. His 11.5 tackles for loss lead the Volunteers. The figure is also tied for second among the nation's interior defenders. Plus, he's doing so against SEC competition. Gilliam may not be the biggest or longest defensive tackle. However, his constant energy and general disruptiveness have caused him to skyrocket throughout the evaluation process, with the potential to be the first defensive tackle off the board in April.

No matter what, NFL teams will be enamored with quarterback prospects presenting elite physical tools. Everyone in the league believes they can develop tantalizing traits, though the ability to actually to do so is scattershot at best.

South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers is this year's candidate with elite physical traits but developmental-level performance. An argument can easily be made in his favor that he presents as much natural upside as any prospect available in 2027.

The 21-year-old is now in his third season as a starter for an SEC program. He's been highly erratic throughout that time. However, the 6'3", 238-pound signal-caller is a top-notch athlete with a howitzer strapped to his right shoulder. He's run for 90 or more yards in four of the Gamecocks' nine contests, including 147 during an overtime loss to a ranked Kentucky Wildcats squad. Plus, the ball comes out of his hand with such easy velocity.

Sellers' biggest issues have been with his footwork, consistency as a passer and inability to throw with anticipation. However, he has made incremental improvements in all three areas, particularly during South Carolina's ongoing four-game winning streak.

As long as Sellers doesn't completely melt down during the final stretch, he has the traits and growth potential to be viewed as a first-round option. At best, he could climb to QB2 behind Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker with a stellar finish to his senior campaign.

The term "unicorn" is often overused in today's sports vernacular. An individual should present a unique skill set of some sort to earn the designation. A 6'5", 210-pound safety prospect with top-notch ball skills fits the bill.

As a redshirt sophomore after two mostly forgettable seasons with the Oregon Ducks, Kingston Lopa wasn't on many radars upon transferring to the University of California. His five interceptions during the Golden Bears' first three games certainly caught everyone's attention.

A concussion basically cost Lopa two games, but he's been back on the field for Cal's last three contests.

The safety's vision to read the ball in front of him and quickly trigger is exceptional. His length and athleticism to cover significant ground both sideline-to-sideline and downhill are obvious.

Lopa continues to develop as a tackler, and he must also get a better feel for his angles. Even so, a potential eraser along the back line with his range and length is something not currently seen at the professional level.

All-Pro Kyle Hamilton quickly comes to mind when thinking of bigger, playmaking safeties. However, Lopa currently lacks the versatility and physicality Hamilton showed coming out of Notre Dame.

Keep in mind, Hamilton only had four interceptions during his final two collegiate seasons. Thus, Lopa's ball skills will drive his value, especially if he gets back on track late in the campaign.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills 2026 Midseason Awards and Superlatives
articles.summary: With the trade deadline in the rearview, the Buffalo Bills officially enter the second half of their 2026 campaign this Sunday against the New York Jets.
articles.body:
With the trade deadline in the rearview, the Buffalo Bills officially enter the second half of their 2026 campaign this Sunday against the New York Jets.

Buffalo sits atop the AFC at 7-1, but the record masks a turbulent first two months.

Before the stretch run begins, here are my midseason awards and superlatives.

Impossible to overthink this one and justify anyone else. Allen is heavily in contention for his second league MVP award. He's consistently a hero with his arm and his legs and is the anchor of the league's highest-scoring offense.

Offensive Player of the Half-Year: RB James Cook

This is based on the idea that Allen can't win both. Cook's 814 yards in eight games trail only Kenneth Walker III in the conference. He leads all AFC backs in touchdown and first-down runs. It appears he's gotten past a ball-security issue, as he remains the tone-setter of this high-powered offense.

Defensive Player of the Half-Year: Edge Greg Rousseau

The 26-year-old former first-round pick has taken off under Jim Leonhard. He's the only player in football with at least eight sacks and three forced fumbles. The edge rusher has become a legit contender for NFL Defensive Player of the Year.

Rookie of the Half-Year: CB Davison Igbinosun

It didn't take long for the second-round selection to steal Maxwell Hairston's starting job opposite Christian Benford. He's still prone to lapses and penalties, but is improving rapidly. The staff already trusts him to go one-on-one with guys like Justin Jefferson.

Comeback Player of the Half-Year: K Tyler Bass

After missing the entire 2025 season due to hip and groin issues, Bass has gone a perfect 19-for-19 thus far in 2026.

The second-year Kentucky product certainly upped his game as his rookie season progressed, but he's taken it to a completely different level in 2026. Walker is a terror as a pass-rusher and overall game disruptor, even if he still disappears at times.

Most Underrated Player: WR Khalil Shakir

Shakir, who has a team-best 31 receptions, always seems to come through when really needed. He edges out fellow wideout Keon Coleman, as both are overshadowed by Allen, Cook and DJ Moore at the offensive skill positions but are heavily relied on.

Tylan Grable and Greg Gaines are strong candidates here, but Johnson has 210 receiving yards on just 97 snaps. He's averaging a ridiculous 12.4 yards per target, which leads all qualified backs by a margin of more than four yards.

Trench Warrior of the Half-Year: C Connor McGovern

Dion Dawkins has lacked consistency, Alec Anderson has been adjusting to a starting role, while Spencer Brown has been dealing with a balky back. Meanwhile, the veteran center and the guard to his right, O'Cyrus Torrence, have been mauling from the inside all year long.

Most Disappointing Player: CB Maxwell Hairston

But only because C.J. Gardner-Johnson is off the roster and thus ineligible. Regardless, Hairston has fallen out of favor fast and hard as a sophomore first-round pick. The lowest-graded defender on the roster at Pro Football Focus has averaged just 16 snaps per game since losing his starting job after Week 4.

After missing all but three games in 2025, the sometimes-awesome, sometimes-unremarkable Oliver has already missed three more thus far in 2026. It appears the team knows it is going to need to rely more on DeWayne Carter, Landon Jackson or both as the season wears on.

The "What Are We Paying For?" Award: WR Joshua Palmer

Oliver and Bradley Chubb are strong candidates here, too, but at least they are basically every-down guys when healthy. Even before a hamstring injury landed him on injured reserve, the veteran Palmer had caught just four of the 12 passes thrown his way while dropping three. All while continuing to enjoy his three-year, $30 million contract.

The Hero-or-Zero Award: TE Dalton Kincaid

It's funny: Kincaid is averaging 53.6 yards per game, but he has yet to record a game between 40 and 80 yards. He's had three massive performances with at least 13 fantasy points. He's had five anonymous showings with fewer than four fantasy points. Nothing in between.

The second-year blocking specialist has been on the field for 42 percent of Buffalo's offensive snaps but is tied for the team lead with five penalties. It's been a disappointing sophomore campaign overall. It all starts with the yellow flags.

Breaking Down Most Underrated Prospects in 2027 NFL Draft 🏈

Moore hasn't been healthy much this season, but when he's on the field, his presence has changed how defenses handle this Buffalo attack. He already has a few elite performances under his belt despite a nagging shoulder injury. He's dropped zero passes on 32 targets.

We've already talked about Walker, and Oliver's ceiling is undeniable when he's healthy. T.J. Sanders was one of the best players on the field in a critical prime-time victory over the Rams. Gaines, Carter and Landon Jackson have all had their share of nice moments supporting the primary cogs.

Most Underrated Position Group: Cornerback

Christian Benford has recovered from a poor start to become one of the steadiest cover guys in the league over the last few weeks. It's a remarkable turnaround, just as Igbinosun has flourished with his aggressive style and Dee Alford has found his footing. Hairston is an afterthought, but one hell of a No. 4 corner. Don't forget about Tre'Davious White, either.

Top Second-Half Breakout Candidate: LB Dorian Williams

It's already happening. The momentum is building for the 25-year-old, who started his fourth season slowly but has now become a versatile piece in the middle of an emerging young defense.

articles.title: In 2021, Matthew Stafford sold his Michigan waterfront mansion for $6 million; his move to Los Angeles changed everything
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford sold his Bloomfield Township lakefront home in August 2021 for $6 million, according to Zillow.
articles.body: Matthew Stafford sold his Bloomfield Township lakefront home in August 2021 for $6 million, according to Zillow. That was $500,000 below his original asking price. The sale came months after the Detroit Lions traded him to the Los Angeles Rams for Jared Goff and three draft picks. Stafford won a Super Bowl that winter and an MVP award four seasons later. The house was the last link to a city that never gave him a playoff win. The timeline shows how cleanly one chapter closed and another opened.Why Matthew Stafford sold his Michigan mansion for $6 millionStafford and his wife, Kelly, bought the property at 1867 Long Pointe Drive in 2013 for $3.5 million and renovated it in 2016. It sits on about 1.27 acres on Upper Long Lake, with a huge infinity pool and a temperature-controlled wine cellar. The listing called it “Michigan’s most magnificent estate.”The first listing came in May 2020 at $6.5 million. Kelly Stafford said then that nobody should read anything into it, and Matthew told reporters he loved being a Lion. The timing still raised eyebrows, because trade chatter was already in the air.The second listing arrived in January 2021, after the quarterback and the team agreed to part ways. Same price, very different meaning. For a family that had spent years in the area, the sale carried real weight, and Kelly later thanked Michiganders for their support, saying “There really is no other place like it.”The house sold in August for $6 million. A discount of about 7.7 percent is modest on a property this size, and Crain’s Detroit Business listed the sale among the priciest in Michigan that year. Stafford seemed to value speed over squeezing out the last dollar.How the trade to Los Angeles changed Stafford’s careerThe Lions drafted Stafford first overall in 2009, and he spent twelve seasons in Detroit. He broke passing records, played through injuries and won plenty of regular-season games. He also reached the playoffs three times and lost every game. His record as the Lions starter was 74-90-1.The trade came together on January 30, 2021, just before his 33rd birthday. Detroit received Goff, a 2021 third-round pick and first-round picks in 2022 and 2023. Detroit’s own rebuild, under new general manager Brad Holmes and coach Dan Campbell, began with that haul. The Rams wanted a bigger arm to run Sean McVay’s offense.The fit showed up right away. Stafford threw for 4,886 yards and 41 touchdowns in 2021, and he paired with receiver Cooper Kupp, who won the receiving triple crown. The money moved just as fast. The Staffords bought a 15,000-square-foot home in Hidden Hills, a gated enclave in the San Fernando Valley, for $19.6 million. Selling at $6 million and buying at $19.6 million tells you how final this move was.Did the Super Bowl run prove the trade right?Yes, and fast. In twelve years with Detroit, Stafford never won a playoff game. Within four weeks of the 2021 postseason, he won four. The Rams beat Arizona in the wild-card round, Tampa Bay on the road and San Francisco in the NFC title game. Then, on February 13, 2022, they beat Cincinnati 23-20 in Super Bowl LVI at their own SoFi Stadium. Stafford’s go-ahead touchdown pass to Kupp came with 1:25 left, and Kupp took home MVP honors.Fairness matters here. Detroit did not fail him alone, since he spent years throwing to Calvin Johnson. But the Rams were built to win immediately, with Aaron Donald and Von Miller on defense, while the Lions were deep in a rebuild. Stafford changed addresses and walked into a roster with a high floor.That is the real lesson of the trade. Quarterbacks rarely change a team’s fortunes alone, yet the right quarterback in the right system can change how fast a good roster wins.Where Stafford and the Rams stand in 2026Stafford’s story did not stop at one ring. In 2025 he led the NFL with 4,707 passing yards and 46 touchdowns, threw only eight interceptions and won his first MVP award. The Rams lost the NFC Championship Game at Seattle on January 25, 2026, and the question became whether he would keep playing. In May, he answered with a one-year extension through 2027.He has also become more than a veteran stopgap. Rookie Ty Simpson, a first-round pick in 2026, is learning behind him, which signals that the Rams see Stafford as the starter, not a bridge.This season has been bumpier. The Rams entered with Super Bowl expectations, then stumbled in the opener and later lost to Buffalo in overtime. Fox Sports wrote in mid-October that the team needed more from its quarterback. Even so, on October 25 he threw three touchdown passes in a 35-21 win over Las Vegas and became the franchise’s career leader in touchdown passes.Detroit has done fine without him, too. Goff led the Lions to a 15-2 record in 2024. Neither side lost this trade, but only one got a championship parade.Stafford is 38 and signed through 2027. The Rams have until then to turn a record-setting quarterback into a second ring.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Patrick and Brittany are investing millions in children growing up in the same communities that shaped their own lives.
articles.summary: For Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, one of their most meaningful investments may have little to do with football or business.
articles.body: For Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes, one of their most meaningful investments may have little to do with football or business. The couple's $1.625 million commitment to Boys & Girls Clubs of America carries a personal connection, particularly for children in East Texas. Through their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, they helped create an opportunity for up to 300 young people to attend club programmes without paying membership fees. The initiative also reflects Brittany's own childhood experience and raises an important question: How much can access to a safe, supportive environment change a child's future?Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $1.625 million commitment supports 300 childrenThe partnership, announced on October 4, 2023, brought together the couple's foundation and Boys & Girls Clubs of America. Its multi-year commitment covers Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse, communities that have played important roles in their lives.One part of the agreement has a direct focus on East Texas. Boys & Girls Clubs of East Texas, through The Mentoring Alliance, was set to provide scholarships for up to 300 children to attend its programmes each year at no cost.This support could make a difference for families who struggle with the cost of organised activities and after-school care. Instead of worrying about membership fees, eligible children can gain access to supervised programmes, activities and opportunities to develop new skills.The local organisation also highlighted the importance of the contribution. Kevin East, president and CEO of Mentoring Alliance, said, “Patrick and Brittany have deep roots in East Texas and share our passion for kids and families in this community. We couldn’t be more excited to partner with the Mahomes. Their contribution to our scholarship fund will be a tremendous blessing to the working families we serve, giving hundreds of kids access to affordable, quality programs.”Brittany Mahomes' childhood connection gives the initiative a personal meaningThe programme carries an added emotional connection because Brittany Mahomes previously attended a Boys & Girls Club. That experience helped shape the couple's decision to support an organisation that provides young people with guidance and resources beyond the classroom.Patrick also spoke about why the partnership matters to their family.“We are truly excited to partner with Boys & Girls Clubs of America by investing in the future of children. Kids who attend a Club, like Brittany once did, are provided with the necessary tools and resources to help this generation not only thrive but lead with compassion and purpose.”Brittany shared a similar commitment, saying, “This meaningful partnership will expand opportunities for kids everywhere, and the places that have positively impacted Patrick and me. We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others.”The foundation's contribution also supports facility improvements at Boys & Girls Clubs in Greater Kansas City and Lubbock, with locations recognising the partnership by carrying the 15 and the Mahomies name.For the children in East Texas, however, the most important part may be the opportunity itself. Access to a supportive space, caring adults and activities can give young people room to discover their interests and build confidence. The lasting measure of the Mahomes family's commitment will ultimately be the opportunities these children receive and the difference those experiences make in their lives.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Commanders Troll Jameis Winston, Giants with 'Who Let the Dogs Out' Photos After Viral Video
articles.summary: In addition to stealing a 24-21 win over the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium, the Washington Commanders got to have fun at the expense of Jameis Winston afterward.
articles.body:
In addition to stealing a 24-21 win over the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium, the Washington Commanders got to have fun at the expense of Jameis Winston afterward.

Winston entered the game for a third-and-1 sneak attempt late in the fourth quarter and used "who let the dogs out" as part of his snap cadence, so naturally the Commanders had to mention it in their victory post on X.

Winston's sneak attempt came with 3:53 remaining in the fourth quarter and the Giants trying to preserve a 21-17 lead. He was initially awarded a first down, but the Commanders challenged the spot and it was overturned to no gain.

The Giants took a delay of game and punted the ball away. Washington scored two possessions later on Stefon Diggs' 32-yard touchdown catch with 57 seconds remaining to get the win and move two games back of the Giants for first place in the NFC East.

articles.title: Jameis Winston’s quirky trick against Washington Commanders backfires on New York Giants
articles.summary: The New York Giants needed just one yard to keep the ball.
articles.body: The New York Giants needed just one yard to keep the ball.Instead of running a play, they tried to trick the Washington Commanders into crossing the line early - so that a penalty would give the Giants a free first down. But instead, the Commanders did not fall for it and stayed completely still.Because the Giants never actually snapped the ball, they ran out of time on the play clock, were penalized five yards and had to kick the ball away to the other team.Conclusion? Jameis Winston’s quirky trick against the Washington Commanders miserably backfired on the New York Giants!Was Jameis Winston’s Who Let the Dogs Out stunt necessary?Sometimes, it’s better to keep Jameis Winston’s colorful side limited to his off-gridiron endeavors. When he brings that personality onto the gridiron, the trick can backfire. Now, the Giants have one more loss on their record.This is not all on Jameis Winston, of course. But singing, “Who Let the Dogs Out” during such a crucial moment in the football game?It’s supposed to confuse defenders. It’s supposed to make the defense unsteady on its feet. But no, their hearts and minds might have wandered back to their childhoods - when they would dance to the iconic song! The song might have relaxed them completely.They might have been more dumbstruck than confused. Some Commanders players even laughed out loud.Yes, it was funny. But was it necessary? Jameis Winston has a beyond colorful, larger-than-life personality off-gridiron, but was it necessary to bring that personality onto the gridiron? Especially when the stakes are high and the game is on the line - deciding brink?The goal was simple - to draw the Washington defense into jumping offsides. How did Winston attempt to achieve that? By singing Baha Men’s 2000 hit ‘Who Let the Dogs Out’, originally written by Anslem Douglas.But the song did not make Washington’s defense budge an inch. The Commanders maintained their diehard discipline, as if they had been prepared for exactly this kind of stunt from Winston at such a crucial moment!Washington gained seven points after Jameis Winston’s stuntLate in the fourth quarter, the New York Giants were comfortably leading 21-17 with just 3 minutes left on the clock.Facing a tough fourth-and-1 on their own 11-yard line, Giants quarterback Jameis Winston tried to trick the Washington Commanders by singing “Who Let the Dogs Out” before the snap. The plan backfired, resulting in a Giants penalty and forcing them to punt.Although Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels threw an interception shortly afterward, New York couldn’t capitalize and had to punt again. Washington got one final chance, and did they make the best of it? Absolutely!Helped by a costly penalty against the Giants’ defense, Jayden Daniels threw a 32-yard touchdown pass to veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs with just 57 seconds left on the clock. A successful extra point sealed a 24-21 comeback win for the Commanders.So, was that “Who Lets the Dogs Out” stunt really necessary?Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: If you've ever wondered how quarterbacks come up with some of their cadences, Jameis Winston offered some insight into his process after incorporating "who let the dogs out" into his snap count on Thursday night.
articles.body:
If you've ever wondered how quarterbacks come up with some of their cadences, Jameis Winston offered some insight into his process after incorporating "who let the dogs out" into his snap count on Thursday night.

Following the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders, Winston told reporters he tried it out once in practice because it "just had a nice ring to it."

Winston attempted to draw Washington's defense offside on a fourth-and-1 play late in the fourth quarter by incorporating the slogan popularized by the Baha Men.

Unfortunately for Winston and the Giants, the cadence didn't cause Washington to bite and New York would end up punting the ball away.

The Commanders got the win on Stefon Diggs' go-ahead touchdown catch in the final minute of regulation to improve to 3-5-1 this season.

articles.title: 'Baby Kobe' Jayden Daniels Hyped by Stefon Diggs After Game-Winning TD Pass vs. Giants
articles.summary: After orchestrating his fifth career game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime in the Washington Commanders' 24-21 win over the New York Giants, Jayden Daniels earned a new nickname from one of his teammates.
articles.body:
After orchestrating his fifth career game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime in the Washington Commanders' 24-21 win over the New York Giants, Jayden Daniels earned a new nickname from one of his teammates.

Stefon Diggs, who caught the game-winning 32-yard touchdown pass with 57 seconds remaining, hyped up Daniels to reporters as "Baby Kobe" in reference the Los Angeles Lakers legend.

Daniels' reputation for stepping up in clutch moments was born during his rookie year when he led four late-game comebacks in the regular season to propel Washington to a 12-5 record.

The momentum carried over into the playoffs that year when Daniels led two fourth-quarter scoring drives, including a 10-play drive that took the final 4:41 off the clock and culminated with Zane Gonzalez's walk-off 37-yard field goal in a 23-20 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Thursday night was Daniels' first game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime since that victory over the Bucs. Some of that can be attributed to injuries because he only played seven games last season and missed two games this season due to a dislocated elbow.

Daniels previously came close to engineering a late comeback in Week 6 against the San Francisco 49ers, but his efforts came up short in a 23-17 defeat.

Thursday's victory was crucial for the Commanders because a loss would have dropped them four games back in the loss column for first place in the NFC East and given the Giants the head-to-head tiebreaker.

Instead, Washington has the tiebreaker advantage and is within two games in the loss column for the top spot in the division. The Commanders also have the easiest remaining strength of schedule among all four NFC East teams with just three games left against teams that currently have winning records.

The Giants, by comparison, have three of their next four games against the Jacksonville Jaguars, 49ers and Seattle Seahawks.

Next up for the Commanders might be their most difficult game remaining against the Cincinnati Bengals in a Monday Night Football showdown on Nov. 23.

articles.title: Ex-Notre Dame and current Washington Commanders QB Sam Hartman to be the next 'Bachelor'
articles.summary: Hartman is currently on the Commanders' practice squad.
articles.body:
"The Bachelor" is featuring a quarterback again.

The ABC dating show announced Friday morning that current Washington Commanders practice squad QB Sam Hartman would be the lead on the show's next season. The 30th season of the show premieres on March 21.

Hartman, 27, has been with the Commanders since he went undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft, largely on the team's practice squad. He has not appeared in a regular season game.

He played collegiately for four seasons at Wake Forest before transferring to Notre Dame for his final season of college football in 2023. Hartman was one of the most productive passers in the country over his final two seasons with the Demon Deacons. In 2021, Wake Forest went 11-3 as Hartman threw for nearly 4,300 yards and 39 touchdowns. He also added 11 rushing TDs that season.

In his only season with the Fighting Irish, Notre Dame went 9-3 as Hartman threw for 24 TDs and eight interceptions.

Hartman is the second NFL QB to lead "The Bachelor" after former Florida and New York Giants quarterback Jesse Palmer. The current ESPN college football analyst — and "The Bachelor" host — was the main character for the show's first season in 2004. Palmer was in his third season with the Giants at the time of the show and played one more season in the NFL before getting into a media career.

Another former QB and current ESPN analyst, Jordan Rodgers, was on "The Bachelorette" and ended up being chosen by JoJo Fletcher, the season's lead.

Palmer, who got married in 2020, did not meet his future spouse in his time on the show, but Rodgers and Fletcher got married in 2022. Perhaps Hartman will follow their lead. Over 20 couples who met on either "The Bachelor" or "The Bachelorette" are currently together.

Sam Hartman is keeping busy between his job as a quarterback on the Washington Commanders' practice squad and now searching for love on national television.

ABC announced on Friday that Hartman will be the star of the new season of The Bachelor premiering on March 21.

Hartman spent six seasons playing college football from 2018 to 2023. He won the starting job at Wake Forest as a true freshman and went on to appear in 48 games over five years.

After the 2022 season, Hartman transferred to Notre Dame for his final year of college eligibility. He was named the starter and led the Irish to a 10-2 record in 12 starts.

Hartman went undrafted in the 2024 NFL draft before signing with the Commanders. His primary role has been on their practice squad, though he has been elevated to the active roster twice. He has yet to appear in a regular season game.

The 27-year-old Hartman will join a long list of athletes to appear on the reality dating show. Jesse Palmer, Arie Luyendyk Jr. and Colton Underwood were all leads on The Bachelor .

Jordan Rodgers and Clay Harbor were both contestants on The Bachelorette . Rodgers won his season and went on to marry Joelle Fletcher in 2022.

articles.title: Arch Manning, CJ Carr Rise on Mel Kiper's New 2027 NFL Draft Big Board Rankings
articles.summary: Quarterbacks CJ Carr of Notre Dame and Arch Manning of Texas have both improved their stock for the 2027 NFL draft recently in the eyes of draft expert Mel Kiper Jr.
articles.body:
Quarterbacks CJ Carr of Notre Dame and Arch Manning of Texas have both improved their stock for the 2027 NFL draft recently in the eyes of draft expert Mel Kiper Jr.

Kiper released his latest big board ranking the top 25 prospects in the 2027 draft, and he had Carr moving up from No. 8 to No. 4, and Manning going from No. 24 to No. 22 compared to his previous rankings.

Carr and Manning were two of the seven quarterbacks in Kiper's top 25, joining Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker (2), Miami's Darian Mensah (7), Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss (20), Missouri's Austin Simmons (21) and Oregon's Dante Moore (23).

The top 10 NFL draft prospects based on Kiper's latest rankings are as follows:

Carr had been behind Mensah in Kiper's previous rankings, but he made an adjustment following Notre Dame's 31-24 win over then-No. 1 Miami last weekend.

The 21-year-old Carr was excellent in that game against a top opponent, going 29-of-40 for 319 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions.

For the season, Carr is completing 67.6 percent of his passes for 2,168 yards, 21 touchdowns and only one pick, making him a strong Heisman Trophy contender.

Manning entered the season as a popular Heisman pick, and although the many ups and downs he has experienced have perhaps knocked him out of the running, he has acquitted himself well recently.

The nephew of legendary NFL quarterbacks Peyton and Eli Manning, Arch has led the Longhorns to three consecutive victories and the No. 6 ranking in the country with a 7-2 record.

Over the past two games against Mississippi State and Missouri, Manning has thrown six touchdown passes and no interceptions. He did throw two picks in the previous win over then-No. 7 Ole Miss, but he also accounted for three total touchdowns.

Manning feels like he could be the ultimate boom-or-bust pick with the range of outcomes stretching from the top quarterback in the 2027 NFL draft to a player who can't establish himself as a consistent NFL starter.

NFL teams in need of a quarterback will have a ton of options at their disposal in the 2027 draft, but there is no clear consensus on who is the best of the bunch.

Mestemaker may be the most popular choice, having maintained his No. 2 overall spot since Kiper's last rankings, but even he is far from a slam dunk to pan out.

One storyline to watch as the draft gets closer is the record for most quarterbacks taken in a single first round. The current record is six, but based on Kiper's rankings, a new record of seven could be possible.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson's 'Challenging' Injury Timeline Updated by Ravens HC Jesse Minter After Thumb Surgery
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between six and 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb, head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Friday.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss between six and 10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb, head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Friday.

"Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal," Minter said. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return."

Jackson's health has been a primary storyline surrounding the Ravens throughout the 2026 campaign.

First, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain. While he returned for Baltimore's Week 8 game against the Buffalo Bills, he exited after his first snap with the thumb injury that required surgery.

To make matters worse, Baltimore lost backup Tyler Huntley to a turf toe injury and had to turn to Joe Fagnano for the rest of the loss to the Bills and the entirety of the following loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The Ravens scrambled and traded for Jacoby Brissett in an effort to weather the storm.

Baltimore is looking to snap a four-game losing streak Monday night against the winless Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson undergoes thumb surgery, expected to be out 6-10 weeks
articles.summary: Jackson needed surgery to repair a broken and dislocated thumb suffered in Week 8 against the Bills.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson could miss anywhere between six-to-10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb suffered against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8 , head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Friday.

Jackson "is doing everything he can" to return this season after undergoing surgery, Minter said, as the 4-5 Ravens continue to battle in a tight AFC North.

"Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8," Minter said . "Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."

"Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8," Minter said .

"Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.

"We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."

Jackson, who had been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury, suffered the injury during his first pass in Week 8, making contact with the hand of Bills linebacker Gregory Rousseau. The quarterback left the game immediately and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve later that week with the hope that he could return later this season.

The Ravens have eight games remaining in the regular season and still have their bye week awaiting them in Week 13. A six-to-10 week recovery timeline certainly allows for Jackson, who reportedly told teammates to " just stay alive ," to return this season. But that could also depend on where the team is in the AFC playoff hunt when he's approaching 100% healthy and ready to play.

With backup Tyler Huntley on season-ending IR with turf toe, the Ravens turned to Joe Fagnano as QB1 after Jackson's injury. The Ravens went and acquired Jacoby Brissett last week from the Arizona Cardinals. He is expected to start on Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Rankings, Box Score Projections for Players with Top Matchups
articles.summary: Week 10 got underway on Thursday night, and another 13 matchups remain on the schedule. The action will pick back up on Sunday morning when the New England Patriots battle the Detroit Lions in Munich.
articles.body:
Week 10 got underway on Thursday night, and another 13 matchups remain on the schedule. The action will pick back up on Sunday morning when the New England Patriots battle the Detroit Lions in Munich.

Fantasy managers are undoubtedly searching for the best matchups heading into the rest of the week's schedule. The fantasy playoffs are right around the corner, and simply leaning on star power may not be an option.

The 2026 season has seen injuries aplenty, and the Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers have the week off.

Here, you'll find some updated point-per-reception (PPR) rankings, along with stat predictions for our favorite matchups.

Matchup to Love: Drake Maye vs. Detroit Lions

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye had a miserable game against the Green Bay Packers in Week 9. He was picked off three times and watched as the Packers built a big early lead. The gap on the scoreboard left the third-year signal-caller abandoning the run.

Maye still topped 21 fantasy points, though, while delivering a high volume of passes in a comeback attempt.

We should see Maye scramble a bit more this week, as New England will be without TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson. It can use Maye's legs to augment the ground game. He has a lot of upside this week against Detroit.

The Lions boosted their secondary by trading for safety Andre Cisco at the deadline, but they have still surrendered the most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks in 2026.

Week 10 Projection: 305 passing yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 45 rushing yards, 1 rushing TD

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Matchup to Love: Chuba Hubbard at New Orleans Saints

Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard only saw 16 carries against a stiff Denver Broncos defense in Week 9. However, he caught four of five targets and finished with a solid 13.6 fantasy points.

Hubbard has become one of the most trustworthy backs in fantasy this season, as he's reached double-digit points in every single game. Even in Carolina's blowout loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, he managed to hit 10.0 points despite logging just seven carries.

The Panthers should lean on Hubbard and the ground game much more in this week's NFC South showdown with the New Orleans Saints. Hubbard should shine.

Coming out of the bye, the Saints defense looked much better against the Cleveland Browns last week. However, New Orleans has still surrendered more fantasy points to opposing running backs than any other team.

Week 10 Projection: 109 rushing yards, 3 receptions, 26 receiving yards, 1 TD

Matchup to Love: Parker Washington at Tennessee Titans

Like the Panthers, the Jacksonville Jaguars will face a divisional foe this week. Against the Tennessee Titans, that should mean a lot of opportunities for top receiver Parker Washington.

Washington has cemented himself as Trevor Lawrence's top target, and he's rewarded fantasy managers more often than not. He only had two catches last week against the Baltimore Ravens but still found the end zone and delivered 14.1 fantasy points.

Expect Washington to have another strong game, as the Jags look to pour it on against a divisional foe with a lackluster secondary.

The Titans have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing receivers than any other team, and they just traded standout safety Amani Hooker early in the week.

Week 10 Projection: 6 receptions, 98 yards, 1 TD

Matchup to Love: Tyler Warren vs. Miami Dolphins

Following a strong rookie campaign, Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren has been disappointing on the fantasy front this season. He reached double-digit fantasy points in four of his first five games, then missed a pair of contests, and hasn't hit double digits since.

However, Warren should be back in the fantasy spotlight. The Colts need him to produce against the Miami Dolphins because they're running out of reliable pass-catchers.

Indy traded wideouts Keenan Allen and Josh Downs ahead of Tuesday's deadline. Warren and running back Jonathan Taylor will be the focal points of their offense moving forward.

The Dolphins have surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season.

Week 10 Projection: 7 receptions, 67 yards, 1 TD
