articles.title: What awaits Fernando Mendoza in his NFL debut? Facing Seahawks' No. 1 defense, Raiders remind rookie he's not 'Spring Fernando'
articles.summary: Mendoza's teammates don't expect perfection from their new leader under center. They do expect resilience, which their 6.5-point home underdog status suggest...
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza didn't "want to talk about myself as a third person."

But the No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft admitted Wednesday that in the Las Vegas Raiders quarterback room, just that sometimes happens.

Raiders quarterback coach Mike Sullivan looks at his rookie and speaks in the third person.

"In the quarterback room, sometimes Coach Sully, he'll reference back to 'Spring Fernando'…" Mendoza told reporters. "It just shows how much improvement there's been, and I'm a lot more confident."

"Spring Fernando" had plenty of proverbial skins on the wall, chief among them a Heisman Trophy and a national championship in his lone season at Indiana. But "Spring Fernando" didn't understand his NFL playbook and teammates as deeply as Mendoza does now, teammates and coaches say. "Spring Fernando" responded differently to blitzes and showed a less advanced command of the huddle; he conceptualized two-minute drills and situational football with less nuance, and he threw the ball less accurately.

None of this, the Raiders say, is a knock on the quarterback whom "you don't draft him unless you feel that way, taking him first overall," head coach Klint Kubiak said. But entering an NFL meeting room for the first time can't compare to observing half a season behind 15-year NFL veteran Kirk Cousins. A first glance at the playbook doesn't instill concepts as deeply as running the scout team against an NFL defense each week.

So as the Minnesota Vikings approached the Las Vegas Raiders at the trade deadline about acquiring Cousins, the Raiders faced a decision. What was more valuable: letting Mendoza sit a few more games before handing the reins over, or a third-round draft pick and $10 million in salary credit?

"We had to make a hard decision," general manager John Spytek told reporters. "I mean, we're all kind of staring the future in the face here with Fernando."

On Sunday in Las Vegas, Mendoza will receive his first NFL start. The football gods have not gifted him breaks. The Raiders host the Seattle Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest yards per game in the NFL through nine weeks. Only three defenses across the league have allowed fewer points. Adding to the chess match nuances, as well as the heightened emotions: Kubiak will be scheming against the team whose offense he coordinated to the Super Bowl nine months prior. Play-callers will know each other intimately. Kubiak hopes Mendoza does not feel pressure rests on his shoulders alone.

"We have an awareness of his situation and being in his first game," Kubiak said. "However, we're not peeling back anything and we're going to go do what the whole team does best, all 11. …

"He's got to do his job and not worry about a whole lot else. Everybody does their 1/11th, and everything around him elevates their play."

Raiders' best bet is taking pressure off Mendoza. But are they capable?

When the 2016 NFL season kicked off, the Dallas Cowboys arrived at the "Sunday Night Football" opener with a rookie quarterback.

Incumbent starter Tony Romo had fractured a bone in his back during a preseason game, after second-string quarterback Kellen Moore broke his ankle during training camp. So the Cowboys' fourth-round pick got the start. Dak Prescott completed 25 of 45 pass attempts for 227 yards, no touchdowns and no turnovers as the Cowboys lost 20-19 to the New York Giants.

Dallas would go on to win its next 11 games and 13 overall en route to the NFC's No. 1 seed. Along the way, the Cowboys decided their recipe: Don't ask Prescott to air it out and play hero ball in every moment.

Fast forward to Mendoza, and former Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett recommends a similar strategy.

"You try to take the burden off of him…" Garrett, now on NBC's "Football Night in America" studio show, said Wednesday on a conference call. "Quiet the game down for him, try to get the running game going early, high-percentage throws early, move the quarterback. Try to get him to be 5-for-5 [passing] before he even thinks about it to get into the flow of the game. Those aren't easy things to do, but that has to be your objective.

"Once he gets his legs underneath him and he's got a good look in his eye, then you start trying to attack the defense a little bit more."

Mendoza has some traits playing in his favor for that proposed game plan. He was highly accurate last year in college, completing 72% of his pass attempts even as he led all FBS passers averaging 10.78 air yards per attempt. The 23-year-old Mendoza is more mobile than his 38-year-old predecessor. And the Raiders, who rank fifth in passing through nine weeks under Cousins, have a handful of reliable targets in the passing game — beginning with tight end Brock Bowers (whose alignments more often position him like a receiver than an in-line tight end) and receiver Tre Tucker. The Raiders' offensive line has also pass-protected well, ranking second in pass-block win rate, per ESPN's advanced metric .

Working against Mendoza: the rest of his Raiders surrounding cast and his first opponent. While Mendoza, Kubiak and the locker room emphasized players stepping up to share the load with Mendoza, Cousins was disproportionately carrying the team until he got traded. While Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards and 11th in passer rating, the Raiders' run game has languished with the second-fewest rushing yards per game (71.3) and the fewest rushing yards per attempt (2.89). The Raiders' defense hasn't alleviated the offense's load: No team has allowed more points than the Raiders' 29.8 per game, and no team has allowed more yards per game than the Raiders' 385.4.

Las Vegas has won four games overwhelmingly because of its passing game — and now faces Seattle's No. 1-ranked defense and No. 1 passing defense for Mendoza's first outing. When the Seahawks shuttered the Kansas City Chiefs' otherwise explosive run game last month, Patrick Mahomes and Co. managed just 3 points.

Multiple former offensive play-callers cautioned against translating that into a pass-happy plan.

"You want [his pass attempts] to be in the 20 to 25 [range]," one former NFL play-caller told Yahoo Sports on condition of anonymity. "You don't want the kid to go out there in his first-ever game against the Seattle defense and throw the ball 43 times."

"If you try to go after these guys too early, then you get a lot of negativity happening for the quarterback in the first start of his career [and] it can be tough sledding," Garrett said. "Get him settled. It's OK to punt early. But take the burden off him and get him comfortable."

Raiders on transition from Cousins: Not 'punting on this season'

Mendoza's teammates don't expect perfection from their new leader under center. They do expect resilience, which their 6.5-point home underdog status suggests they may need.

"Everyone has faith in him," Bowers said. "You might have a bad play here and there, but you just got to flush it. And I know he does a good job at that."

In two initial college seasons at Cal, Mendoza completed 66.5% of his pass attempts for 4,712 yards, 30 touchdowns and 16 interceptions. In his third year, at Indiana, that rose to 72% of passes for 3,535 yards, 41 touchdowns and just six interceptions. No one in FBS football last year passed for more than Mendoza's 41 touchdowns and no one was more efficient than his 182.9 rating.

But a national championship moment caught his current teammates' eyes as much as Mendoza's accuracy and precision.

Facing fourth-and-4 with 9:18 to play against Miami, Mendoza tucked the ball and ran upfield for a 12-yard touchdown.

"He lowered his shoulder and ran through the guy for a touchdown," Tucker said. "So that shows the kind of guy we're getting and we're very excited about that. …

"When I put it to him, I feel like there's nothing that he can't do."

Mendoza's preseason play was up-and-down as he completed 25-of-45 pass attempts for 240 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while taking four sacks.

How will he look with the Raiders' starting lineup after running the scout-team offense in recent months?

"I haven't really got too much reps with him, but just whenever they're pulling up tape or whatever, he's just making great throws over and over," running back Ashton Jeanty said. "Accurate, precise, going through his reads. So giving the defense a good look week in and week out over there."

Spytek praised Mendoza this week as having "passed every test," insisting the Raiders' trade of Cousins "in no way signifies that we are punting on this season."

But perhaps the Raiders will measure progress in the coming weeks based not only off game results but also on the development of a young core individually and in concert. How will Kubiak's impressive play-calling look with his new quarterback? Will teammates step up to rally around Mendoza?

No one expects a mistake-free rest of the season.

But one NFC talent evaluator who scouted Mendoza in the preseason pointed to his 35 college starts and 1,008 college pass attempts as indications that Mendoza may transition smoothly.

"These older prospects that have seen a lot of ball, I feel once they start acclimating to the speed of the game, can take off quickly," the evaluator told Yahoo Sports. "I wouldn't be surprised to see him do really well."

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers calls out Pittsburgh Steelers’ biggest weakness before Cincinnati Bengals showdown as Mike McCarthy’s play calling faces scrutiny
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is 6-2 in 2026, but he still yearns for more - his second Super Bowl title in what is expected to be the final year of his NFL career.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers is 6-2 in 2026, but he still yearns for more - his second Super Bowl title in what is expected to be the final year of his NFL career.Even with extra time to rest and regroup during the midseason bye, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is focused on areas where he can still improve.As the crucial Week 10 AFC North showdown against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals approaches, Pittsburgh’s struggles are once again resurfacing - particularly with the wide receivers, red-zone decisions, and head coach Mike McCarthy’s play-calling.Aaron Rodgers vs Joe Burrow in AFC North clashThe 42-year-old signal-caller spoke to reporters Wednesday and acknowledged that winning can sometimes hide problems that can eventually become costly in the playoffs - particularly when the stakes are highest.“I feel like being 6-2 is really good. When you win, sometimes you can gloss over some areas that need improvement if you want to get to where you want to get to, so I think that’s the important thing that experience gives you,” Aaron Rodgers said.He hopes that his team will hold itself to a higher standard so that it can compete in championships in January and February.The upcoming matchup is particularly crucial because the Cincinnati Bengals are also entering Week 10 with a 6-2 record. Sunday’s showdown could determine who takes the lead in the AFC North. Who falls to 6-3 and who flies to 7-2!Mike McCarthy’s overdependence on DK MetcalfAaron Rodgers’ team has failed to convert 50 percent of its red-zone opportunities into touchdowns. This could become a big hurdle against stronger contenders heading into the 2026 playoffs.The Pittsburgh quarterback believes execution is the primary problem. “It’s just execution. There are fixable things, so we’ll fix them and hopefully be better this week,” he said.However, according to TribLIVE News’ Tim Benz, execution is not the problem; the issue lies in head coach Mike McCarthy’s play selection. The Steelers could hand the ball to running backs Jaylen Warren or Rico Dowdle, or opt for the Pat Push.They just need to stop repeatedly calling high-arching end-zone jump balls, or “fade routes,” for veteran wide receiver DK Metcalf. They also need to stop trying to turn tight end Darnell Washington into something he is not by putting him in difficult situations.Pittsburgh’s passing game presents another challenge. Rodgers noted that the Steelers must expect a lot of man coverage and stressed the importance of receivers winning their individual matchups.“We’ve got to get open and win our one-on-ones and get the ball delivered in the proper spot,” he said.The one-time Super Bowl champion hopes Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson return sooner rather than later. He is also looking forward to seeing what Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Max Hurleman can contribute.As for the upcoming matchup vs. Joe Burrow’s Cincinnati Bengals, Rodgers praised Burrow and his two star wide receivers, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.“The Bengals have been playing really well lately. They’ve only lost one since we played them. Joe [Burrow] is having a great year. Those two studs they’ve got [Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins] are having Pro Bowl- or All-Pro-caliber years.So, we know we’ve got to put some points up and handle the environment,” he said. Burrow also had some compliments for the veteran quarterback.Joe Burrow’s praise for Aaron Rodgers ahead of Steelers clashDuring a Wednesday media interaction, Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow spoke about Aaron Rodgers. Burrow was asked about his possibility of Week 10 being his final game vs. Rodgers because then Rodgers could retire in 2027.“He’s one of the greatest that’s ever done it,” Burrow said. “He’s 41 or 42 and still doing it at a high level. I would have trouble calling it quits when I’m still playing like that at that age.So I’ve enjoyed watching him for a long time, and this year, I think he’s playing so well. And, you know, he really played great in the last game we played.Dang! You’re perfect. And made me feel like I had to be perfect the whole time too. And, you know, he’s done that for a long time.”In the first meeting between the Bengals and Steelers this season, Rodgers’ team defeated Burrow’s side 30-27. Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns. Repeating that performance may require Pittsburgh to address its current struggles.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Talks 'Encouragement' in NFC East Title Race After Giants' Loss to Commanders
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones liked what he saw Thursday night when the Washington Commanders came from behind to beat the NFC East-leading New York Giants 24-21.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones liked what he saw Thursday night when the Washington Commanders came from behind to beat the NFC East-leading New York Giants 24-21.

During an appearance Friday on 105.3 The Fan (h/t Jon Machota of The Athletic), Jones discussed the game and its impact on the Cowboys, saying, "It gives us a lot of encouragement as we go forward to one of the biggest games we've had around here in a long time. It's exciting."

Thanks to Washington's win, Dallas moved within 1.5 games of the Giants for the NFC East lead.

It has been a roller-coaster season for the Cowboys, who sit at 4-5, but they are still very much in contention for a division title thanks to the overall weakness of the NFC East.

The Giants had a chance Thursday to put some real distance between themselves and the rest of the division, but Washington came through in the clutch.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels threw a go-ahead, 32-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs with 57 seconds remaining, and cornerback Rasul Douglas picked off Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy to seal the victory.

New York fell to 5-3-1 with the loss, while Washington improved to 3-5-1, bringing it within two games of the Giants and a half-game of the Cowboys.

The Cowboys can draw even closer to the G-Men with a win on Sunday, but that will be easier said than done.

Dallas is hosting the San Francisco 49ers, who have the best record in the NFC this season at 7-1.

However, if the Cowboys can pull off the upset, it could result in them going on a roll, as they have winnable home games against the Tennessee Titans and Philadelphia Eagles on tap the following two weeks.

Meanwhile, the Giants are about to face a tough stretch with games against the Jacksonville Jaguars, 49ers and Seattle Seahawks over three of the next four weeks.

It is anyone's guess how the NFC East will play out over the next several weeks, but there is no question that Washington's win on Thursday significantly improved the chances of both the Commanders and Cowboys when it comes to chasing down the Giants.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Updates Timeline for 18-Game NFL Schedule, Changes to Preseason
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones believes the NFL could move to an 18-game schedule as soon as the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones believes the NFL could move to an 18-game schedule as soon as the 2027 season.

During his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan's K&C Masterpiece show (h/t The Athletic's Jon Machota ), Jones said the 18-game regular season is a possibility to be implemented next season and it would coincide with a reduced preseason schedule.

"It's in everybody's best interest. … I would anticipate that coming," Jones said.

The NFL adopted its current 17-game format starting with the 2021 season as part of the most recent collective bargaining agreement.

The current CBA runs through the 2030 season, so any change to the current schedule format would require a negotiation between the league and players' union.

Commissioner Roger Goodell told reporters in February during his annual pre-Super Bowl press conference there had not yet been any "formal discussions" with the NFL Players Association about expanding the regular-season schedule.

"We have not had any formal discussions about it and frankly very little of any informal conversations," Goodell said. "It is not a given that we will do that. It's not something we assume will happen. It's something we want to talk about with the union leadership."

In a March interview with The Athletic's Mike Jones , newly-elected NFLPA executive director JC Tretter said that player healthy and safety would be a priority for the union in any scheduling changes:

"There are things that are not good for our players that we need to make sure we're protecting them from. And as of right now, those are all subjects of bargaining. The league can't expand past 10 international games. The league's at 17 games in the CBA, that is where we're at, and we're going to make sure we defend our players and their health and safety, because our guys feel they know what this feels like."

Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio reported back in May that expansion to 18 games in time for the 2027 season is "highly unlikely."

The NFL has already announced Super Bowl 62 will be played on Feb. 13, 2028. That could be an indication the league isn't expecting an 18-game schedule because, as Florio noted, adding an extra game would also likely result in teams receiving two bye weeks during the regular season instead of one.

That would stretch the regular season out to 20 weeks, meaning Week 1 would have to be in the final week of August unless the NFL did away with the off-week between the conference championship games and Super Bowl.

It doesn't appear the NFL is eager to do that having previously cited the "enormous logistical challenges involved" with staging a Super Bowl that requires the additional time to put the event together.

Since the NFL introduced the current scheduling format in 2002 with the standalone kickoff game in Week 1, Sept. 4 is the earliest date a game has been played. The 1997 season marks the last time an NFL season has started prior to Sept. 1 when Week 1 was played on Aug. 31.

articles.title: Ravens finally reveal Lamar Jackson's official return timeline and QB could miss rest of regular season
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson faces a 6-10 week recovery from thumb surgery, and the Baltimore Ravens have lost four straight games in a crowded AFC North race.
articles.body: Lamar Jackson's return to the Baltimore Ravens lineup following his surgery to repair a broken and dislocated thumb got a dose of clarity on Friday, but not necessarily a ray of optimism. Following criticism of the club over the fact Jesse Minter was tight-lipped and refused to provide clear details on whether surgery had occurred or what the actual recovery trajectory looked like, the Ravens released a statement from their coach on the matter. Short answer: Jackson is out 6 to 10 weeks. LAMAR JACKSON GOES FROM BEING A PROBLEM FOR 31 NFL TEAMS TO BECOMING A PROBLEM FOR THE RAVENS That is not good news. Jackson suffered the ugly injury to his throwing hand during the first play of a Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. That was on Nov. 1. Jackson underwent the surgery to repair the issue that same week, sources have told OutKick and Fox News Digital. So allow us to do some calendar math: THE WEEK OF THE BACKUP QB IN THE NFL KICKS OFF AS SANDERS, MILTON, MINSHEW, LOCK, AND WENTZ START Six weeks from Nov. 1 would land on Dec. 13, which is Week 14 of the NFL's 18-week regular season. That is the most optimistic view of when Jackson might return. It could be argued it's also the most improbable view because recovering from this injury and surgery on his throwing hand is not easy for a quarterback because after the recovery, there needs to be a regaining of strength and flexibility. The other end of that spectrum is the 10-week recovery period. That one would mean Jackson misses the remainder of the regular season. It also means that the quarterback would not be ready to play until around Jan. 10 which is around when the NFL's wild card round of the postseason begins. (The NFL has not yet released the actual dates of its postseason games). This is all interesting and means things. It means, at worst, the Ravens must rally the remainder of this season and play well enough to make the playoffs to see Jackson back in the lineup again. Checking in with reality, that is unlikely. It's not that Jackson cannot get ready to play again, it's just that there may be no postseason game for him to prepare for because the Ravens have lost four consecutive games, are in last place in the AFC North, and are currently out of the playoff picture. And, yes, the club this week traded for journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett to start until Jackson returns. But Brissett's career record as a starting quarterback is 23-50. No bueno. So let's consider the optimistic outlook, which is Jackson returning by the middle of December. The Ravens have three games between now and Dec. 13 because they have a bye in Week 13. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!y Can the team stay relevant the next three games by breaking a four-game losing skid and not losing sight of the Cincinnati Bengals, Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns in the division? That's the question. "[Jackson] is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said in the team's statement released on Friday. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." They're going to have to do exactly that to make Jackson's return timeline matter at all. articles.title: Rams’ Myles Garrett Makes Confident Statement on DPOY Chances
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett claimed he still believes he can win the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year award. The post Rams’ Myles Garrett...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett boldly claimed he still believes he can win the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year award despite missing seven games due to injury.

Garrett had a one-word response on the Rich Eisen Show when asked if he could still win the award: "Absolutely."

The veteran earned the award in the 2025 season prior to his blockbuster move to the Rams in the offseason, leading the NFL with an all-time record-breaking 23.0 sacks with the Cleveland Browns last season, and also led the league in tackles for loss with 33—the second-most in a single season behind J.J. Watt's 39 in 2012.

Garrett also won the award in 2023, recording 14 sacks while forcing a career-high four fumbles.

Garrett suffered a knee injury during the preseason, but attempted to play through it and made his Rams debut in Week 1's loss against the 49ers.

He was far from his best during the game, failing to record a single tackle during the contest, and the Rams revealed shortly after he was heading to injured reserve to deal with the knee injury. Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery to fix his knee, and sat out for the following seven weeks.

How Did Myles Garrett Perform in His Return Game?

Garrett marked his return to action with an incredibly strong outing against the Washington Commanders on Sunday, logging three tackles—all of which came as sacks. With three sacks, Garret now has the second-highest tally on the team despite missing seven games. He also forced a fumble in the contest, making 2026 the 10th consecutive season in which he has done so.

"Man, it was a weight off my shoulders, just getting back to who I am," Garrett said . "I'm nowhere near where I want to be as far as my performance and things I know I can do and how I can move, but this is a confidence booster for sure."

Garrett's performance helped the Rams to their third consecutive win, bringing them into a tie with the Seattle Seahawks for second place in the NFC West behind the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Their next game comes against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at 1:05 p.m., and the Rams will hope Garrett's addition will help them get revenge on their divisional rival following their loss in Week 6.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Lions Friday injury report: Rhamondre Stevenson, A.J. Brown headline nine questionable
articles.summary: Game statuses for Week 10 in Munich.
articles.body:
The light will be left on for running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver A.J. Brown.

Both starters stand among the New England Patriots' nine questionable to face the Detroit Lions in Germany. Both logged back-to-back limited practices at the FC Bayern Munich training ground while working back from knee injuries.

Fullback Reggie Gilliam, tight end Cameron Latu, offensive linemen Walter Rouse and Greg Van Roten, cornerback Charles Woods, and safeties Kevin Byard III and Brenden Schooler also carry questionable game designations for head coach Mike Vrabel's 5-4 side of the aisle.

Here's the final injury report ahead of Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at Allianz Arena.

The Patriots ruled out three prior to the overseas flight. Henderson will be missing his third consecutive game in the backfield due to an illness . In addition to the No. 38 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, New England will also go without starters at left guard and outside cornerback due to knee injuries that arose during last weekend's 45-27 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium.

As for head coach Dan Campbell's 6-2 contingent, the Lions also previously ruled out three.

G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return)

After sitting out Wednesday's walkthrough back in Foxborough, Stevenson made the trip to Munich. That was the case for the lead running back despite reportedly facing a multiweek absence because of a knee tendon issue. He's ahead of schedule amid a season that has brought 128 combined carries and catches along with 657 yards and four touchdowns from scrimmage.

Brown, meanwhile, has been listed as a partial participant for three straight sessions. After landing on injured reserve in September due to a high ankle sprain, the June trade acquisition out wide missed the past two weeks worth of practices and starts because of a flared-up knee. The three-time Pro Bowler and All-Pro has totaled nine receptions for 101 yards thus far into his Patriots stay.

New England also has a pair of candidates to return from injured reserve before Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline for moves. And an open spot on the 53-man roster, too. Van Roten, a veteran of 147 NFL games along the interior line, had his 21-day practice window open last week after residing on IR due to a hamstring injury . An upgrade to full participation has followed while a fellow Patriots guard progresses through the league's concussion protocol. And at fullback, Gilliam, who arrived on a three-year deal in March, was designated to return from a knee injury in the hours before the flight across the Atlantic Ocean.

But offensive captains in tight end Hunter Henry and right tackle Morgan Moses will officially go without game designations after managing foot ailments.

articles.title: Patriots takeaways from Germany: What Mike Vrabel said about A.J. Brown playing in Munich
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel said he felt 'pretty good' about A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson after seeing them practice
articles.body:
MUNICH – After making the trip to Munich, will A.J. Brown play on Sunday against the Detroit Lions?

That was the big question facing the Patriots on Friday. Temperatures dipped into the low 40s as the team held a full 90-minute practice at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. After flying into Munich on Thursday, and holding a 60-minute walkthrough, Mike Vrabel's team picked up the pace.

The Patriots coach said he felt "pretty good" about the status of A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson after watching the two players at Thursday's practice.

"So, let's go through today and see where that goes and then meet with (trainer) Jim (Whalen) and meet with players," Vrabel said.

Brown has played in three of nine games this season. The Pro Bowl receiver missed four weeks in a row after suffering a high ankle sprain in the team's regular-season opener in Seattle. After returning, and playing twice in five days, Brown's been dealing with a nagging knee injury.

The receiver missed two weeks of practices and the Patriots matchups against Miami and Green Bay. Brown returned to practice on Wednesday before flying with the team on Thursday.

"I think the more that we can get everybody back, I think the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team," Vrabel said when asked about having Brown at practice. "And one guy certainly doesn't make the difference, but it's certainly the more that we can get guys back. It's exciting that the pieces can start to build and come together. So, you know, we'll see where things go today. And hopefully, you know, those guys that haven't been with us or maybe got hurt last week, that could be available."

In three games, Brown's caught nine passes for 101 yards. He'd be a huge boost for Drake Maye and the offense, if healthy. After dealing with two different injuries, Vrabel was asked if the team needed to protect Brown from himself when it comes to how much they play him when he does return.

"I mean, again, we just have to try to see where things go and how they feel, and we got to trust them a little bit, how they tell us and also have a plan for each and every guy," Vrabel said. "I think it's kind of see how it goes."

In their final injury report, Brown was ruled questionable for Sunday's game against Detroit.

Here are the top takeaways from the Patriots' second day in Munich:

If Brown plays, it'd be a huge boost for the offense. The same can be said if Rhamondre Stevenson is cleared to play on Sunday.

The running back suffered a knee injury last weekend against Green Bay. On Monday, ESPN and the NFL Network reported Stevenson would miss weeks due to his injury. However, Stevenson flew with the team to Munich and practiced the last two days.

Stevenson's presence here has been surprising. Vrabel said the veteran is working hard to play and admires his attitude.

"I think we're just always looking for guys that are looking for ways in as opposed to ways out," Vrabel said. "At this point in the season, 10 weeks straight without a bye, there's pretty much nobody out there that's 100% and we have to realize that. We have to recognize that. But we also have to find ways to do our job and Rhamondre's one of those players that is looking for a way in."

Stevenson was with his teammates at the start of practice, but was not wearing his jersey. The team listed him as limited on Thursday.

Considering he's the Patriots leading rusher and his impact in the passing game within blitz pickup, it'd be huge for the offense if Stevenson could play this weekend.

The running back was listed as questionable in the team's final injury report.

The Patriots running back room is running short. TreVeyon Henderson didn't travel with the team this week due to his illness.

Last week, Henderson revealed that he'd been dealing with an undiagnosed neurological condition. Vrabel said he didn't have a timeline for the speedy back's return.

"I talk to TreVeyon every day and just like everybody else that's not available, he's working hard to get back and when that is, I don't know," Vrabel said. "I don't have a timetable. But I love my interactions with him, I love talking with him."

If Henderson is going to be out for the foreseeable future, the Patriots could place him on the non-football injury list. The issue, however, is that the team is running out of injured reserve-return slots. Every team gets eight per season. The Patriots already used five with Romeo Doubs and Alijah Vera-Tucker eligible to return after the bye week.

Vrabel was asked if they're weighing putting Henderson on the reserve list due to the limited options they have.

"Yeah, those are things that we work through. You know, we're very conscious of that and we're just until we absolutely need the spot and we haven't had that necessarily pinch and still also just have to try to figure out when he may be available," Vrabel said. "But then also you're right, we have guys coming back from, from injured reserve or designated to return. So there's a lot of things that we have to weigh through with the roster."

The Patriots lost their last two international matchups in London and Frankfurt. In both cases, the Patriots flew Thursday night and held one practice on Friday before the Sunday matchup.

This week, Vrabel opted to change that by having the team fly in a day early to get two practices in to help ease the jetlag.

"You know, just having done this a few times and maybe how you feel coming over here on Friday and what you're able to get done. I felt like we wanted to try to do a little bit more maybe than had been done in the past on a Friday," Vrabel said. "So, get here a day early to be able to walk through. Come over here last night, walk through. I thought helped guys just get moving a little bit, get the airplane and get the flight out of us and then got up this morning. It's been a regular Friday and we'll get going on practice here pretty soon."

This week has been a homecoming for Lorenz Metz . The Patriots offensive tackle was born in Neuötting in Bavaria, Germany.

Metz has had an interesting journey to the NFL as he didn't play football until 18. Now, he's close to his hometown and practicing at the training facility for the soccer team he grew up rooting for.

"It's a surreal feeling," Metz said. "I grew up about an hour from here. FC Bayern was the team for me—Thomas Müller, (Manuel) Neuer, all those Bayern players were my idols. To be standing on this pitch now—it's just incredible."

Metz played in the German Football League for the Kirchdorf Wildcats in 2017. The next year, he moved to the United States and played collegiately at Cincinnati. In 2023, he entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent. He's been on the practice squads in Chicago and Tampa Bay before joining the Patriots practice squad last season.

Metz said he started to watch the NFL when Germany first started broadcasting the games. At the time, the Patriots and Tom Brady were the most popular.

"I think it was around 2012 when they started broadcasting regular-season games on free-to-air TV in Germany," Metz said. "Back then—2012, 2014, 2016—the Patriots were right at the top, thanks to Tom Brady. They were the team everyone knew; everyone knew Tom Brady."

This week, Metz gathered his teammates for a team dinner in Munich. He wouldn't reveal what restaurant they went to, but said he wanted to give Patriots teammates a true feel of the food and culture that he grew up in.

"I wanted to give my teammates a taste of Bavarian culture," Metz said. "We'll definitely have some beer steins, and there will be traditional Bavarian dishes like roast pork and schnitzel."

Milton Williams has seen enough. Now, it's time for his teammates to pay up.

Over the last two games, the Patriots defensive linemen have been called for offside penalties seven times. The group had four penalties against Miami and then three last weekend against Green Bay.

For that reason, Williams has instituted a fine for his teammates. Every time a player gets called for a defensive offside penalty, they owe Williams $1,000. At the end of the season, the money will be donated to the Patriots support staff.

"I put in fines this week. $1,000 fine for whoever jumps offside," Williams said. "I had a couple early, early in the season. And I feel like we talk about it, but it's not enough consequences to come with it other than hurting the team. So hurt your pockets."

articles.title: 'Elite' Ben Johnson Praised as NFL Exec Predicts Caleb Williams, Bears Could Win NFC North 'Easily'
articles.summary: Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson has quickly made a name for himself as one of the best coaches in the NFL. Although the Bears are in the midst of a competitive battle for the NFC North title, at least one league executive believes that Johnson's coaching could lead Chicago to the top.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson has quickly made a name for himself as one of the best coaches in the NFL. Although the Bears are in the midst of a competitive battle for the NFC North title, at least one league executive believes that Johnson's coaching could lead Chicago to the top.

"Chicago is the best-coached," an AFC executive told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . "[Johnson's] elite. One of the best in the NFL and only in Year 2. One of the best offenses week-in and week-out, as well. Defense is solid. Caleb [Williams] just has to play within the scheme and they will win it easily, I believe."

The Bears are currently holding a slim division lead with a 7-2 record, but the division is far from decided. The NFC North has a .736 winning percentage, which is the best through nine weeks since the 1970 merger, according to ESPN's Bill Barnwell . All four NFC North teams have at least six wins, and the Green Bay Packers are currently in last place with a 6-3 record.

Johnson is just in his second year at the helm in Chicago, but he immediately transformed a downtrodden Bears organization into a legitimate Super Bowl contender. The Bears won the division with an 11-6 record in Johnson's first season with the team, and they're now looking to win the title in back-to-back seasons for the first time since 2006.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has also made significant strides in his development under Johnson. The third-year passer has reduced his sack rate and improved his completion percentage since his difficult rookie season.

The Bears will enjoy a bye in Week 10 before kicking off the second half of their season against the New Orleans Saints. Chicago still has four divisional games remaining on its schedule. The Bears have yet to face the Detroit Lions, and they will look to avenge losses against the Packers and the Minnesota Vikings.

articles.title: Brock Purdy's MVP Case Hyped by NFL Execs as 49ers Push for NFC West Title
articles.summary: NFL executives believe San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy may have the best case to win the 2026 AP NFL Most Valuable Player award, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
NFL executives believe San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy may have the best case to win the 2026 AP NFL Most Valuable Player award, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

"He's playing a position at a high level," an NFC executive told Fowler. "He's putting it all together."

Another league executive said Purdy could win because the MVP is "a narrative-driven award" and San Francisco "looks like the best team in the NFC" despite dealing with an injury-riddled roster. The 49ers sit atop the conference with a 7-1 record, and they currently rank as the league's third-best scoring offense and sixth-best scoring defense.

Heading into the 2026 season, much of the preseason buzz surrounding the NFC West revolved around the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks and the revamped Los Angeles Rams. Yet, San Francisco has jumped out to a comfortable lead over its division rivals.

Purdy isn't unfamiliar with being overlooked. The fifth-year quarterback became the last selection of the 2022 NFL Draft when he was selected with the No. 262 pick. Since then, he has led the 49ers to two division titles, two NFC championship games and one Super Bowl appearance.

Purdy has 1,980 passing yards with 17 touchdowns and five interceptions through eight games. He's also added 201 rushing yards and two scores on the ground.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson refuses to give up on the Ravens' season as team reveals brutal 6-10 week recovery timelin
articles.summary: The Baltimore Ravens have finally provided a clearer picture of Lamar Jackson's injury, and the latest update is not exactly what fans wanted to hear.
articles.body: The Baltimore Ravens have finally provided a clearer picture of Lamar Jackson's injury, and the latest update is not exactly what fans wanted to hear. The $260 million quarterback is expected to miss several more weeks after suffering a serious thumb injury, leaving Baltimore facing an uphill battle as the 2026 NFL season moves forward. However, there is one thing Jackson apparently does not want anyone to forget: He is not ready to give up on his season just yet.Ravens reveal worrying 6-10 week recovery timeline for Lamar JacksonJackson's injury dates back to Baltimore's November 1 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Things went wrong almost immediately for the Ravens when their franchise quarterback injured his right thumb on the opening offensive play.His throwing hand collided with a Bills defender while he was attempting to deliver a pass to wide receiver Zay Flowers. Jackson eventually left the game, and further examinations revealed a fractured and dislocated thumb.The injury was serious enough for Baltimore to place him on injured reserve on November 5, guaranteeing that he would miss at least four games. But the situation became even more concerning when head coach Jesse Minter provided an update on November 13. According to Minter, injuries of this nature typically require around six to 10 weeks to heal, especially following surgery.That timeline could keep Jackson away from the field for a significant portion of the remaining regular season. While the Ravens have not officially ruled him out for the entire campaign, the latest announcement makes his immediate return increasingly difficult.Lamar Jackson is not ready to call it quits on the seasonDespite the disappointing medical update, Jackson has reportedly maintained a positive outlook about his chances of returning. According to reports, the quarterback has communicated his determination to teammates and encouraged them to keep fighting while he works through his recovery.His reported message was simple: "Just stay alive." It is a particularly important message considering Baltimore's current position. Jackson wants his teammates to keep the Ravens in playoff contention so that he has something to return to if his recovery goes according to plan.A six-week recovery could potentially give him a chance to return during the final stretch of the regular season. However, a 10-week timeline could push his comeback into the postseason, provided Baltimore manages to qualify. For now, there is no confirmed return date, and the Ravens will have to be patient with their star quarterback.Ravens face another challenge without their $260 million quarterbackJackson's absence could hardly have come at a worse time for Baltimore. The Ravens have struggled throughout the season and entered this stretch with a 4-5 record following four consecutive defeats. Things have become even more complicated with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley also dealing with a season-ending turf-toe injury.Baltimore subsequently brought in veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett to help stabilize the offense while Jackson recovers. The pressure is now on Brissett and the rest of the roster to keep Baltimore's playoff hopes alive.For the Ravens, the immediate priority is getting through the coming weeks without their franchise quarterback. But for Jackson, the bigger goal remains making it back before the season is over. The latest update has certainly made that challenge much harder. articles.title: Raiders' Decision to Trade Kirk Cousins, Start Fernando Mendoza Detailed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders reportedly planned to keep veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins beyond Tuesday's NFL trade deadline before ultimately handing the reins to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders reportedly planned to keep veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins beyond Tuesday's NFL trade deadline before ultimately handing the reins to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that the Minnesota Vikings were initially rebuffed in their earlier attempts to land Cousins before the Raiders eventually relented.

"As recently as last weekend, there were people in that organization who wanted to stick to the plan -- to keep Cousins past the trade deadline and hold off on playing Mendoza a few more weeks, maybe even until after their Week 13 bye," Graziano stated. "The Vikings called the Raiders about Cousins prior to last weekend, but it wasn't until after Sunday that they felt there was a chance Vegas would trade him."

Kirk Trade Result of Vikings' 'Desperation'

The Vikings sent a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders to acquire Cousins, who had played six seasons in Minnesota from 2018 to 2023. The 38-year-old is expected to stabilize things under center amid star quarterback Kyler Murray's hamstring injury and backup Carson Wentz's struggles.

Mendoza said Cousins "had me with open arms and has taught me so many things, whether it's film study, how to operate as a starting quarterback, all the different multifaceted approaches that have made him so successful, he has shared with no restrictions or constraints." It's clear that he feels he had the proper guidance before making his first career start.

Mendoza will need all the confidence he can muster when he leads the Raiders (4-5) against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks (5-4) on Sunday.

articles.title: George Pickens Drops Viral Quote Updating Injury Status for Cowboys vs. 49ers amid Hamstring Issue
articles.summary: After missing Week 9 due to a hamstring injury, George Pickens had a unique way of letting everyone know he plans to be back for Sunday's marquee matchup featuring the Dallas Cowboys hosting the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body:
After missing Week 9 due to a hamstring injury, George Pickens had a unique way of letting everyone know he plans to be back for Sunday's marquee matchup featuring the Dallas Cowboys hosting the San Francisco 49ers.

Asked after Friday's practice if he will be on the field, Pickens had this response: "Tell your wife or your girl to turn the TV on, and she'll see me on the field."

The Cowboys listed Pickens as a limited practice participant on Wednesday and Thursday. He originally popped up on the injury report with an unspecified issue in Week 7, but he played the next two games.

Things got to the point where Pickens was unable to go against the Indianapolis Colts. Dallas survived without him in a 27-23 win thanks to CeeDee Lamb's 195-yard effort.

It certainly sounds like Pickens will be back as the Cowboys look to get a much-needed win against a 49ers team that currently sits atop the NFC standings with a 7-1 record.

articles.title: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston leaves broadcasters floored with absurd snap count: 'What is he doing?'
articles.summary: Jameis Winston sang "Who Let the Dogs Out" in his snap count trying to draw Washington offside, leaving Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit stunned.
articles.body: In one of the most critical moments of the New York Giants' loss, Jameis Winston decided to bust out one of the most absurd snap counts of all time. Winston, who was trying to draw the Washington Commanders offside on fourth-and-1 on the Giants' own 11-yard line, decided to start singing in his cadence. "Set, we good, we good, we good. Get ready, get set, hut one, hut two, hut three. Who let the dogs out, woof, woof, woof, woof," Winston said in his snap count. articles.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown Teases Joining Germany's Flag Football Team for 2028 LA Olympics
articles.summary: Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has an opportunity to play football in Germany this week, but he's hoping to represent the country on an even bigger stage in the future.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has an opportunity to play football in Germany this week, but he's hoping to represent the country on an even bigger stage in the future.

St. Brown told reporters on Friday that he wants to play flag football for Germany's national team at the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles, according to The Associated Press' Ken Maguire .

"I would love to play for the German national team for the flag Olympics, that would be something off my bucket list that I've done," St. Brown said during his press conference.

The All-Pro wide receiver has deep ties to the country. His mother, Miriam, was born in Leverkusen, Germany, where St. Brown spent many summers. St. Brown is fluent in German and hosts annual youth football camps in Germany during the offseason, according to MLive's Benjamin Raven .

There's a qualifying tournament scheduled a few weeks before the Olympics begin, which the 27-year-old wide receiver said he would attend if he can work out potential scheduling conflicts with the Lions training camp.

Jona Winkel, Germany's flag football director of coaching, declined to say if there's been contact with St. Brown, Maguire reported, but didn't seem opposed to the idea.

"In our experience, receiver is by far the position that allows the fastest transition from tackle to flag football," Winkel said.

St. Brown will have an opportunity to play his first NFL game in Germany on Sunday when the Lions face the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich.

articles.title: Curt Cignetti taunts the CFP committee and then gets obliterated, Cam Skattebo freezes & Gracie Hunt checks in
articles.summary: Curt Cignetti fires back at the CFP committee over Indiana's five-spot drop, but fans were quick to point out the Hoosiers' zero ranked wins.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Well, here we are. Friday. We've made it! The weather man tells me we're supposed to drop down to the 40s tonight here in Florida. We've got a full weekend of FOOTBALL in front of us. Thanksgiving is 13 days away. I missed a meeting yesterday because Outlook was broken and I couldn't access the calendar with the Zoom link. What a pleasure. Who has it better than us right now? Nobody! We're rolling. Let's get after it. Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Curt Cignetti fires SHOTS at the CFP committee, and then promptly takes on heavy fire from fans in the comments section. HERE'S HOW BAD THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF'S SELECTION COMMITTEE RANKINGS ACTUALLY ARE | IAN MILLER Lordy, these rankings are divisive. Good thing we're expanding! What else? I've got plenty of reader mail from the week to get to now that my email is no longer under a cyberattack (allegedly!), and did Cam Skattebo cost the Giants the game last night? I know I know — he scored twice. But did y'all see what he did, or didn't do, on that third down play late in the fourth quarter? Wild. We'll dive in. Grab you a sweatshirt if you're down here in FRIGID Florida, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap! Curt Cignetti asks the committee a simple question It's a Friday and we've got a lot to get to, so let's get this class started and see if we can get outta here a few minutes early ... Once again, a Big Ten coach has the SEC on his mind. Last weekend, it was Illinois' Brett Bielema, who said his team would be ranked in the top-15 if they were in the SEC. It's a fair point until you remember that Bielema went ... checks notes ... 11-29 in the SEC over his five seasons at Arkansas. That's a tough sell. WE NEED TO ABOLISH THE CFP SELECTION COMMITTEE AFTER YET ANOTHER EMBARRASSMENT | IAN MILLER The latest shot at the committee came from defending champ Curt Cignetti, who certainly has more street cred than Beilema. When Cig talks, folks listen. Doesn't mean he's right, but they at least don't laugh. Here's what Cignetti had to say after the Hoosiers dropped five spots in this week's rankings even though they were on a bye week: What happened with Skattebo here? "Bad losses don't count anymore? 😂😂😂😂😂😂 Are first downs still 10 yards?🤡🤡🤡" Thoughts? Look, I don't know who, exactly, Cignetti is singling out here. No. 1 Georgia, which lost to an unranked Auburn team a few weeks ago? No. 6 Texas? The Longhorns have lost to Florida (yuck) and Oklahoma (double yuck). Either way, it's an SEC team. Here's the problem ... Indiana hasn't exactly faced a gauntlet this season. The Hoosiers have one loss — against Ohio State — and needed overtime to beat Michigan and Minnesota. The SEC is just better than the Big Ten this year ... by a lot. It's a down year for the Big Ten. It happens. The committee is almost certainly punishing Indiana for the schedule compared to Texas or Georgia. Fair or not, that's what they're doing. The always levelheaded folks on social media were QUICK to point that out: Yeah, it's just a tough look to chirp and also have zero ranked wins this season. Zero. That could very well change tomorrow as Indiana faces No. 18 USC. I assume the Hoosiers will win that game because USC under Lincoln Riley never meets the moment. Ever. But should they lose? It'll be open season when the next batch of rankings come out next week. OK, let's leave Bloomington and head to New Jersey, where the Giants lost a game they should've won last night partly because Cam Skattebo appeared to ... do nothing? ... on a critical third down QB sneak: Christmas decorations & Gracie Hunt! I watched it live and was truly baffled. What in the world is going on here? Some folks on the internet think Skattebo was a decoy. OK? That still doesn't explain why he just sat there for two seconds while Jameis was fighting for his life trying to gain an extra two inches. Did he just ... forget to move? Seriously, that's what it looks like to me. Did he zone out? It sounds like an absurd thing to even think, but this is Cam Skattebo we're talking about. He's a bit out there, if you hadn't noticed. And don't get me wrong — I love Cam Skattebo. I'm a huge Skattebo guy. I bet on him to score a touchdown last night, so I owe him the whopping $22 I won if I ever see him. But it was still ... odd. Just odd. OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL. First up? Earlier this week, I asked everyone when it was acceptable to put up the Christmas decorations. Because it's a divisive topic, I received 14,000 responses. From Greg in Amarillo: I will put up the Christmas decorations while or when the weather is nice, AFTER Halloween, of course, give them a test light, but they don't get turned on regularly until Thanksgiving weekend. The inside of the house, including the tree, doesn't go up until Thanksgiving weekend. From Gary B: When in doubt go old school. As a kid growing up in the 70's everybody would start decorating for Christmas after Thanksgiving. It was corporate greed that tried to change that to Halloween. From Jon C: My family tradition is to put up decorations the weekend after Thanksgiving. Plenty of ballgames to "watch" while decking the halls and trimming the tree (artificial). And from Chris B: Hey, Zach — The lights go out on Black Friday, because who wants to leave the house that day anyway? By 5:00 our house looks like a used car lot. So, I have an admission to make that I'm not proud of ... Our house is decorated for Christmas. My wife yanked all the Halloween stuff down last weekend (against my wishes), so our house was just in purgatory for days. It wasn't decorated for Halloween. We don't have a ton of fall decor. And there were boxes and bins everywhere. I couldn't take it anymore. I knew I didn't want to make two trips to the attic, so I decided to bring the Halloween stuff up, and take the Christmas stuff down at the same time. articles.title: Kirk Cousins Named Vikings QB1 Over Carson Wentz vs. Packers After Trade at NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Kirk Cousins will officially make his return to the Minnesota Vikings Sunday night in Green Bay.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins will officially make his return to the Minnesota Vikings Sunday night in Green Bay.

Cousins will start for the Vikings against the Packers just five days after he was traded from the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Kevin O'Connell announced Sunday.

Cousins was acquired in the wake of a hamstring injury to Kyler Murray, who O'Connell said Wednesday is still considered week-to-week.

He will start in place of Carson Wentz, who was listed as limited with an ankle injury earlier this week but was a full participant in Friday's practice.

O'Connell said Wednesday the goal of the coaching staff was to get Cousins "comfortable and allow him to play for us this Sunday."

As of Friday, O'Connell said he was impressed by the command of the Vikings' system Cousins had demonstrated "in a pretty short amount of time."

"I cannot give him enough credit for coming in here, how he's gone about the week," O'Connell said. "Both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, working extremely hard, using all the time we possibly can.

"It's been really impressive, what he's been able to do, and just the command and just getting right back in the huddle, with a lot of guys he's played with but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed by."

Cousins was off to his best season start since his injury-limited 2024 campaign with the Atlanta Falcons prior to the trade, completing 64.1 percent of his passes with 2,340 passing yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in nine games with the Raiders.

O'Connell noted this is the third time he has gotten the opportunity to coach Cousins, who he previously worked with as quarterbacks coach with Washington and earlier in his head coaching stint in Minnesota.

The Vikings will hope that familiarity will help Cousins, who last played for Minnesota in 2023, adjust quickly enough to help his team snap a two-game losing streak despite losing several key players to injury.

O'Connell said four players, including two pass-catchers in wide receiver Jauan Jennings and tight end T.J. Hockenson, had been ruled out for Sunday's matchup. Jordan Addison is also questionable with a thumb injury.

Justin Jefferson could see an even more significant workload than usual as the Vikings, which scored just 21 combined points in their last two outings, work toward a more productive outing in Cousins' return.

articles.title: Titans' Robert Saleh Talks 1st Matchup vs. Jaguars' Liam Coen Since Viral Video of Altercation
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh insisted there isn't any lingering animosity between him and Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen from their viral postgame spat last season.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh insisted there isn't any lingering animosity between him and Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen from their viral postgame spat last season.

"Liam's great, man," Saleh told reporters on Friday. "We've had plenty of interactions. And the whole thing was ... [a] little misunderstanding, poor words on my part. But they're doing a great job, they really are. I love what they're doing offensively. They've definitely got an identity. And then [defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile] on the other side. Just overall as an organization, they've done a really nice job."

The issue stemmed from comments Saleh made prior to a matchup against the Jaguars last season. Saleh, who was the San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator at the time, said Coen's coaching staff had "legally, a really advanced signal-stealing type system where they always find a way to put themselves in an advantageous situation," per NFL writer Kevin Patra .

Saleh insisted his comments were meant as a compliment, but Coen didn't interpret them that way. After the Jaguars' 26-21 win, Coen and Saleh had to be separated after a heated midfield exchange. In a video that captured the interaction, Coen could be heard telling Saleh, "Keep my name out of your mouth."

Although the two coaches haven't coached against each other since then, they both claimed to have cleared the air before the NFL's annual league meetings in April, according to ESPN's Michael DiRocco .

The Titans will hope to spoil the Jaguars' quest for the AFC's top seed when the two teams meet for a divisional bout at Nissan Stadium on Sunday.

articles.title: 5 of the unluckiest plays in sports history to revisit in honor of Friday the 13th
articles.summary: From Leon Lett's Super Bowl fumble to the Kick Six, these five unlucky plays prove Friday the 13th has nothing on sports history's cruelest moments.
articles.body: Friday the 13th. A day synonymous with bad luck and people who genuinely believe walking under a ladder might ruin their entire existence. Over the centuries, sports have proven a twisted sense of humor. Bad luck runs rampant. You can practice your entire life to hone your skills, execute a play almost perfectly, and still end up on the wrong side of a moment so ridiculously unfortunate that it feels like someone upstairs is playing a practical joke. And in honor of Friday the 13th, we're counting down five of the most unlucky, bizarre and downright cruel plays in sports history. DUKE'S BEATDOWN OF NC STATE INCLUDED A MUST-SEE MISSED FIELD GOAL RETURNED FOR A 109-YARD TOUCHDOWN 5. The Kick Six: Alabama's Worst Nightmare (2013) Imagine being the No. 1 team in college football, having national championship aspirations and watching your season take a devastating turn because of a missed field goal. Welcome to Alabama's nightmare. With the 2013 Iron Bowl tied at 28 and just one second remaining, Nick Saban sent freshman kicker Adam Griffith onto the field to attempt a 57-yard field goal against Auburn. What could possibly go wrong? Griffith's kick fell short, landing in the hands of Auburn's Chris Davis, who was standing in the end zone specifically for this possibility. Davis proceeded to sprint 109 yards for a touchdown as the Auburn crowd erupted into absolute pandemonium and stormed the field. The Crimson Tide didn't just lose a football game. They watched their hopes of a third consecutive national championship disappear as Davis sprinted down the sideline. 4. Bill Buckner: The Ground Ball That Haunted Boston (1986) For 86 years, the Boston Red Sox couldn't win a World Series. And for a long time, their fans blamed a certain trade involving a certain baseball player with certain significance, named Babe Ruth. The infamous "Curse of the Bambino" had become part of Boston sports folklore, and the 1986 World Series provided perhaps its cruelest chapter of that saga. Leading the New York Mets 3-2 in the series, Boston was one out away from winning its first championship since 1918 during Game 6. Then everything fell apart. The Mets tied the game in the 10th inning, and with the winning run on second base, Mookie Wilson hit a slow ground ball toward Red Sox first baseman Bill Buckner. It should have been a routine play. Instead, the baseball rolled directly between Buckner's legs, allowing Ray Knight to score the winning run. Game over. The fat lady had sung. The Mets won Game 7, and Buckner's error became one of the most infamous moments in baseball history. To be fair, Boston had already blown its lead before Buckner's mistake, and the Red Sox still had another game to win the championship, but whether you want to call it poor concentration or bad luck, it's one of the most brutal plays you'll ever watch, unless you're a Yankees or Mets fan. YANKEES INFIELDERS COLLIDE, ALLOWING METS TO SCORE GAME-WINNING RUN IN DRAMATIC COMEBACK 3. The Double Doink: The Sound Bears Fans Can't Unhear (2019) There are missed field goals. There are heartbreaking missed field goals. And then there's whatever supernatural, if you will, nonsense happened to Chicago Bears kicker Cody Parkey during the 2018 NFL playoffs. On Jan. 6, 2019, the Bears trailed the Philadelphia Eagles 16-15 in the final seconds of their NFC Wild Card matchup. Parkey lined up for a 43-yard field goal that would send Chicago into the divisional round. The kick went up. DOINK. The football struck the left upright. DOINK. Then it bounced off the crossbar, falling into the end zone. The Bears' season was over. To make matters even more painful, Eagles defensive lineman Treyvon Hester had gotten a fingertip on the football, meaning the kick was officially ruled blocked. Parkey had already hit the uprights four times in a single game earlier that season, making this an almost comically cruel conclusion. One doink is unfortunate. Two doinks on the same kick, with your season hanging in the balance is about as unlucky as you can get. VANDERBILT PULLED OFF THE MOST IMPROBABLE LAST-SECOND VICTORY YOU'LL EVER SEE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL 2. José Canseco: The Headbutt Home Run (1993) If Friday the 13th had an official baseball highlight, this would be it. On May 26, 1993, Texas Rangers' outfielder José Canseco was tracking a deep fly ball hit by Cleveland's Carlos Martínez. Canseco drifted back toward the warning track, positioned himself near the wall and prepared to make what appeared to be a fairly ordinary defensive play. Instead, the baseball struck him directly on the noggin and sailed over the outfield fence for a home run. Canseco didn't just fail to make the catch. He somehow transformed a fly ball into one of the most embarrassing home runs in MLB history. It was comical and unlucky at the same time. Canseco got one baseball to the dome and a lifetime of internet humiliation. 1. Leon Lett: The Super Bowl Touchdown That Never Was (1993) There are few things more embarrassing than celebrating a touchdown before actually scoring it. We've seen far too many bonehead plays where players drop the ball before the goal line. Just ask former Dallas Cowboys defensive lineman Leon Lett. During Super Bowl XXVII against the Buffalo Bills, Lett recovered a fumble and began rumbling toward the end zone for what appeared to be an easy defensive touchdown. The Cowboys were already dominating the Bills, and Lett was about to add another six points to the scoreboard. It would have been his lone touchdown in his career. There was just one tiny problem. He forgot that the play wasn't over. As Lett approached the goal line, he slowed down and began holding the football away from his body in celebration. Meanwhile, Buffalo receiver Don Beebe sprinted after him like his life depended on it, caught Lett just before the goal line and knocked the football out of his hand. The ball rolled through the end zone for a touchback. Lett went from Super Bowl glory to an all-time blooper. The good news? Dallas still won the game 52-17. The bad news? More than three decades later, people still remember the defensive lineman who managed to fumble away a touchdown while celebrating it. And as if the football gods weren't finished tormenting him, Lett became the central figure in another bizarre play later that year when he touched a blocked field goal in the snow against the Miami Dolphins, allowing Miami to recover and eventually kick the game-winner. Two legendary football blunders in one calendar year? Yikes. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Sports are supposed to reward preparation, execution and talent. But every once in a while, the sports gods decide to throw a wrench into that equation. Happy Friday the 13th, sports fans. Watch out for black cats, avoid walking under ladders and, whatever you do, hold onto the football until you're actually in the end zone.

articles.title: Kirk Cousins named Vikings' starting QB for Week 10 matchup vs. Packers
articles.summary: After acquiring the veteran in a trade last week, head coach Kevin O'Connell has confirmed that Cousins will get the start over Kyler Murray.
articles.body:
Days after acquiring Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline, the Minnesota Vikings will officially have the veteran quarterback start this week.

Head coach Kevin O'Connell announced Friday that Cousins will be the team's starting QB for Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. Cousins gets the start with quarterback Kyler Murray out with a hamstring injury.

"Cannot give him enough credit for coming in here, how he's going about the week," O'Connell said in a press conference. "It's been really impressive, what he's been able to do. Just the command and getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with, but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed by."

Cousins, who played for Minnesota from 2018-2023, was reunited with his old team in a blockbuster trade with the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday, right before the NFL trade deadline . The Vikings brought in Cousins as a more viable alternative to backup QB Carson Wentz, who has struggled even more than Murray.

Minnesota has one of the most dominant defenses in the league, allowing just 14.5 points per game. But its offense has not been able to keep up, threatening to waste the Vikings' league-best defense with preventable losses.

Even with Murray's injury, which O'Connell has said is week-to-week, the arrival of Cousins will make the 29-year-old quarterback Minnesota's backup for now. Cousins will be running the show going forward after a solid start to the season with Las Vegas, leaving behind rookie Fernando Mendoza to start for the Raiders .

The team announced Thursday that Cousins will go back to wearing No. 8, the number he wore in his previous stint with the team. (Safety Jakobe Thomas, who was wearing the number, will wear No. 6 instead.)

articles.title: Patriots Defender Institutes New Fine System for Teammates Who Commit Penalties Amid Struggles
articles.summary: New England Patriots defensive tackle Milton Williams revealed that he implemented a $1,000 fine for any defender who commits an offsides or encroachment penalty, with the money going to the team's trainers.
articles.body:
New England Patriots defensive tackle Milton Williams revealed that he implemented a $1,000 fine for any defender who commits an offsides or encroachment penalty, with the money going to the team's trainers.

"I put in fines this week," Williams told reporters Friday (0:14 mark). "$1,000 fine for whoever jumps offsides."

"I had a couple early in the season and I feel like we talked about it, but it's not enough consequences that come with it other than hurting the team," he added.

The Patriots have committed seven offsides or encroachment penalties throughout their past two games (h/t ESPN's Mike Reiss ).

During New England's 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 9, Green Bay was able to pick up three first downs due to Patriots penalties.

New England owns a 5-4 record this season as it attempts to defend its AFC title.

Williams has continued to operate as a key piece of the Patriots' defensive front, racking up 21 tackles, three tackles for loss, two quarterback hits and one sack in nine games. He's also amassed 20 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus .

The Patriots will look to bounce back from the loss to Green Bay in their next game, a matchup with the Detroit Lions in Germany on Sunday. Kickoff is at 9:30 a.m. ET.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker, George Pickens, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 10
articles.summary: One of the most consistent fantasy football performers in 2026 has suddenly become an injury risk for Week 10.
articles.body:
One of the most consistent fantasy football performers in 2026 has suddenly become an injury risk for Week 10.

Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker missed Friday's practice with tightness in his groin.

Walker will now be one of the most-watched players in terms of his injury status between now and Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable.

As for George Pickens, well, he made it quite clear he'll be on the field for the Dallas Cowboys.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 10.

Kenneth Walker sat out of the Chiefs' Friday practice due to a tight groin.

Walker, who is listed as questionable, is currently second in the NFL in rushing yards and tied for ninth in rushing touchdowns. He's run for over 100 yards in five of his eight games.

Walker would obviously be a huge miss for the Chiefs offense for their Week 10 road trip to Atlanta, if the groin issue doesn't get better before kickoff.

Emmett Johnson is a name all fantasy players should know for Sunday in case Walker can't play.

Johnson, a rookie out of Nebraska, would be in line to earn the bulk of the carries against an Atlanta rushing defense that's allowed over 100 yards in four of the last five games.

There's likely already been a rush to the waiver wire to add Johnson since the Walker news broke on Friday afternoon.

Walker's former team, the Seattle Seahawks, is worth targeting on the waiver wire with Jadarian Price. Seattle faces Las Vegas' league-worst rushing defense that allows 151.2 rushing yards per game.

Ollie Gordon, who has had at least 16 carries in each of the last four games, is worth a waiver-wire add as well. Gordon and the Miami Dolphins face an Indianapolis Colts team that gives up 137 rushing yards per contest.

George Pickens delivered an all-time quote when he asked if he'll play on Sunday.

Pickens missed the Cowboys' Week 9 clash with the Colts due to a hamstring injury.

The Cowboys will be happy to have him on the field again in Week 10 for the clash with the NFC West-leading San Francisco 49ers.

The 49ers pose a tough matchup for anyone right now, but with Pickens on the field, Dak Prescott at least has both of his top pass-catching options available to him.

Pickens' return likely means Ryan Flournoy's fantasy value will drop. He caught two balls for 53 yards last week with Pickens out.

If you don't like the matchup for Pickens, Houston's Tank Dell and New England's Demario Douglas are two of the best waiver-wire additions available because of the roles in their respective offenses.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s owned Cleveland Guardians face $105 million payroll challenge as proposed salary floor threatens spending strategy
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s growing connection to Cleveland baseball could face an unexpected financial test.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s growing connection to Cleveland baseball could face an unexpected financial test. The Kansas City Chiefs star joined the Cleveland Guardians’ ownership group as a minority investor in May 2026, adding a new chapter to his relationship with his hometown. However, a proposed Major League Baseball salary floor could force the franchise into a major spending rethink. With Cleveland operating on one of baseball’s smallest payrolls, the proposed changes could put pressure on its long-standing approach to building a competitive team without spending heavily on established stars.Travis Kelce’s Guardians face a major payroll challenge under MLB proposalAccording to a November 9 report by Sports Business Journal, the Cleveland Guardians are among 12 MLB franchises that would need to make substantial financial adjustments to meet the proposed salary floor. MLB has suggested a $180.2 million floor for the 2028 season, although the figures remain projections rather than final requirements.The financial gap is particularly striking for Cleveland. The franchise reportedly operated with an estimated $74.5 million payroll last season, according to Spotrac. Reaching the proposed threshold would require more than $105 million in additional spending.A newer MLB calculation based on 2026 Competitive Balance Tax payrolls also places Cleveland among the teams facing the biggest adjustments. Its payroll stood at approximately $92.6 million, leaving an $87.6 million gap against the proposed floor. The difference reflects the use of separate payroll measurements and seasons.For Travis Kelce, who grew up supporting Cleveland teams, this development puts an important business issue in the spotlight. His investment gives him a stake in the franchise, but he is a minority investor rather than its controlling owner. The proposed changes could test the financial priorities of the entire ownership group.David Blitzer’s growing role could shape the Guardians’ futureCleveland has built its reputation around developing young talent, making smart trades and finding value without competing with baseball's wealthiest teams.The franchise has "learned to survive but thrive as a small-market team thanks to good player development and a smart front office."However, that strategy could become harder to maintain if MLB introduces mandatory spending requirements.Owner Paul Dolan has traditionally followed a conservative financial approach. Meanwhile, minority owner David Blitzer could gain greater influence over the club's future. Blitzer purchased a reported 35% stake in June 2022, with an option to become majority owner after the 2027 season.The report raises questions about whether Dolan's approach will change, noting, "unless owner Paul Dolan has strayed from his conservative financial path entering his 28th year of ownership, minority owner David Blitzer could be playing a much bigger role in running the team in the near future."The Dolan family is still expected to retain a stake in the franchise regardless of what happens next. As Hoynes noted, "No matter what transpires in the next few years, the Dolan family is expected to keep a share in the Guardians."With Travis Kelce now part of the ownership group, Cleveland's financial future carries another interesting dimension.
